Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they decided to play hide and seek. Timmy found a really good hiding spot behind a big tree. He giggled quietly to himself as he watched his friends search for him.

Suddenly, Timmy heard a loud laugh coming from his friend Johnny. Johnny had found him! Timmy's body felt warm and happy as he ran out from behind the tree. They all laughed and played together until it started to get dark outside. Timmy's mom called him in for dinner and he went inside with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore. One day, he was playing with his friend Johnny when they saw a big mountain with smoke coming out of the top. 

Johnny said, "Wow, Timmy! Look at that big mountain! Do you think it's a volcano?"

Timmy replied, "I don't know, Johnny. Let's go measure it and see how tall it is!"

So, they ran over to the volcano and tried to measure it with their hands. But it was too big! They needed a special tool to measure it. 

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and an alert went off. It was the volcano! It was going to erupt! They quickly ran away and found safety. From then on, Timmy and Johnny knew to be careful around volcanoes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cozy blanket that she loved very much. One day, her friend Timmy came over to play. He saw Lily's blanket and said, "I wish I had a blanket like that. I'm envious!" 

Lily replied, "You can borrow my blanket if you want. We can share it together." Timmy was happy and they both snuggled under the blanket. 

After a while, Lily said, "Let's add some pillows to make it even more comfy!" They both giggled and added some pillows to the blanket. They talked and laughed under the blanket until it was time for Timmy to go home. 

As Timmy left, he said, "Thanks for sharing your blanket with me, Lily. It was so cozy and warm!" Lily smiled and said, "Anytime, Timmy. Sharing is always fun!"

Ben and Lily like to play with their dog, Spot. Spot is a large dog with black and white fur. He likes to run and jump and chase balls. Ben and Lily have a leash for Spot, so they can take him to the park.

One day, Ben and Lily decide to race with Spot. They put the leash on Spot and go to the park. They find a big field with a lot of grass. Ben says, "I will race with Spot to that tree. Lily, you count to three and say go."

Lily nods and says, "Okay. One, two, three, go!" Ben and Spot start to run as fast as they can. Lily watches them and cheers. Spot is very fast and pulls the leash hard. Ben tries to keep up, but he trips and falls. He lets go of the leash. Spot keeps running to the tree.

"Spot, stop!" Ben shouts. He gets up and runs after Spot. Lily runs after Ben. They see Spot at the tree, barking at a squirrel. The squirrel runs up the tree and chatters at Spot. Spot jumps and tries to catch the squirrel. He does not see Ben and Lily coming.

Ben and Lily reach the tree and grab the leash. They pull Spot away from the tree. Spot whines and wags his tail. He wants to play with the squirrel. Ben and Lily say, "No, Spot. Bad dog. You have to stay with us."

They walk back to the park entrance. Ben and Lily are tired and dirty. They look at each other and laugh. They say, "That was a fun race, but Spot is too fast for us. Maybe next time we will race with our bikes." They hug Spot and go home. Spot is happy. He likes to race with Ben and Lily. He hopes they will play with him again soon.

Sara and Ben watch the red bird. They are quiet and happy. The red bird watches them too. It flaps its wings and flies away.

"Bye, red bird!" Sara and Ben say.

They wave to the red bird. Then they go back to playing in the field. They have fun in the sun.

They go to the park and find a big tree. They use the tree as a stage. They ask other kids to watch them perform. Some kids say yes and some kids say no.

Tom and Jen start their show. Tom makes funny faces and noises. He trips and falls on purpose. The kids laugh. Jen dances and spins. She wears a pretty dress. The kids clap.

But then, a big dog comes. The dog is not mean, but he is curious. He sees Tom and Jen and runs to them. He jumps on the tree and barks. He wants to play too.

Tom and Jen are scared. They run away from the dog. They leave their stage. The kids stop laughing and clapping. They say, "Where are you going? Come back!"

Tom and Jen hide behind a bench. They feel foolish. They say to each other, "That was not a good show. The dog ruined it. Maybe we should try something else."

They look at the park and see a slide. They have an idea. They say, "Let's pretend to be astronauts. The slide is our rocket. Maybe the dog will not bother us there."

They run to the slide and climb up. They pretend to blast off to space. They forget about the dog and the kids. They have fun.

Lila liked to walk in the park with her dad. She saw many things that made her happy. She saw birds, flowers, dogs and swings. She liked to play and talk with her dad.

One day, she saw something new in the park. It was big and green and had wings and a tail. It was a dragon. Lila was scared and curious. She wanted to see the dragon up close. She asked her dad if they could go near the dragon.

Her dad said no. He said the dragon was not friendly. He said the dragon was envious of the people in the park. He said the dragon wanted to have what they had. He said the dragon could breathe fire and hurt them. He said they had to stay away from the dragon.

Lila was sad and angry. She did not understand why the dragon was envious. She thought the dragon could be nice and share. She thought the dragon could play and talk with them. She thought the dragon could be happy in the park.

She decided to sneak away from her dad and go to the dragon. She wanted to be friends with the dragon. She walked slowly and quietly towards the dragon. She did not see the dragon's eyes glow red. She did not hear the dragon's growl. She did not feel the dragon's breath get hotter. She only saw the dragon's smile.

Anna and Ben are young. They like to play in the snow. They build a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They give him a carrot nose and two coal eyes.

"Look at our snowman!" Anna says. "He is so nice and happy!"

"Yes, he is!" Ben says. "But he is also cold. Let's go inside and have some cocoa."

They run to the house and ask their mom for some cocoa. She pours them two cups and gives them some cookies. They sit by the fire and sip their cocoa.

"Yum, this is so good!" Anna says. "Thank you, mom!"

"You're welcome, sweeties!" mom says. "But don't forget your snowman. He might get lonely out there."

Anna and Ben look out the window. They see their snowman smiling at them. But they also see a big dog running towards him. The dog jumps on the snowman and knocks him down. He bites the hat and the scarf and the carrot nose. He makes a mess of the snow.

"Oh no!" Anna and Ben cry. "Our snowman! He is ruined!"

They run outside and chase the dog away. They try to fix their snowman, but he is too broken. They feel sad and angry.

"Bad dog!" Anna says. "Why did you do that?"

"Go away!" Ben says. "Leave our snowman alone!"

They hug each other and look at their snowman. He is not smiling anymore. He is just a pile of snow.

"Maybe we can build another one tomorrow," Anna says.

"Maybe," Ben says. "But it won't be the same."

They go back inside and finish their cocoa. They hope the dog won't come back. They hope their snowman will be happy again.

Lily was a little girl who liked to see animals. She went to the zoo with her mom and dad. She saw many animals with different tails. She saw a monkey with a long tail, a lion with a fluffy tail, and a peacock with a colorful tail.

She wanted to see more tails, so she ran to the next cage. She saw a large animal with a very big tail. It was an elephant. The elephant was eating some hay. Lily wanted to touch the elephant's tail. She thought it would be soft and fun.

She climbed over the fence and ran to the elephant. She reached out her hand and grabbed the tail. The elephant felt something pull his tail. He was angry. He turned around and trumpeted loudly. He swung his trunk and hit Lily. Lily fell down and cried.

Her mom and dad heard her cry and ran to her. They saw what happened and were very scared. They picked up Lily and hugged her. They said, "Lily, are you okay? You should never touch an animal's tail without asking. It is not nice and it is not safe. The animal might hurt you or get hurt. You should always respect the animals and stay behind the fence."

Lily was sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom and dad. I'm sorry, elephant. I just wanted to see your tail. I didn't mean to make you angry. I learned my lesson. I will never touch an animal's tail again."

The elephant heard Lily's words and calmed down. He nodded his head and waved his tail. He forgave Lily. Lily smiled and waved back. She said, "Thank you, elephant. You have a very beautiful tail. But I will only see it from far away."

The end.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red ball. They would roll it, bounce it, and kick it in the yard. They never wanted to share it with anyone else.

One day, their mom said they had to go to grandma's house for a visit. She told them to pack some clothes and a toy. Tom and Lily both wanted to take the big red ball, but there was only one. They started to fight over it, pulling and pushing and yelling.

"Stop it, you two!" mom said. "You can't both take the ball. You have to separate it. One of you can take the ball, and the other can take something else."

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They both wanted the ball, but they also loved each other. They didn't want to make mom upset. They decided to take turns. Tom said he would take the ball first, and Lily said she would take it next.

They packed their bags and got in the car. Mom drove them to grandma's house, which was far away. It was cold outside, and the sky was gray. Tom and Lily hugged the ball in their laps, feeling warm and happy.

When they got to grandma's house, they ran inside to say hello. Grandma was very happy to see them. She gave them cookies and milk, and asked them what they wanted to do. Tom and Lily said they wanted to play with the ball in the yard.

"Okay, but be careful," grandma said. "It might rain soon. And don't forget to share the ball."

Tom and Lily nodded and ran outside. They played with the ball for a while, rolling it, bouncing it, and kicking it. They had a lot of fun. Then, it was time to switch. Tom gave the ball to Lily, and Lily gave him a hug.

"Thank you, Tom," Lily said. "You are a good brother."

"You're welcome, Lily," Tom said. "You are a good sister."

They smiled and continued to play. But then, they heard a loud thunder. They looked up and saw dark clouds. It started to rain. They ran back to the house, holding the ball.

They got inside and dried themselves. They put the ball on the floor, next to their bags. They went to the living room, where grandma was waiting for them. She had a surprise for them. She had two new toys: a blue car and a pink doll.

"Look what I got for you, Tom and Lily," grandma said. "These are for you to keep. You don't have to share them. You can play with them whenever you want."

Tom and Lily were very happy. They thanked grandma and hugged her. They took their new toys and played with them. They also played with each other, and with the ball. They had a wonderful time at grandma's house. They learned that it was good to separate things sometimes, but it was also good to share them. They also learned that they loved each other very much, and that made them happy.

Tom was a clumsy frog. He liked to hop, but he often fell into the mud or bumped into trees. His friends laughed at him and called him silly. Tom felt sad and wished he could hop better.

One day, he met a wise owl in the forest. The owl said, "I can help you, Tom. I know a magic spell that can make you hop very high and fast. But you have to do something for me first. You have to find a shiny stone and bring it to me."

Tom was curious and excited. He wanted to try the magic spell. He said, "OK, owl. I will find a shiny stone for you. Where can I look?"

The owl said, "You can look in the pond. There are many shiny stones at the bottom. But be careful, Tom. The pond is deep and cold. And there is a big fish that likes to eat frogs. Do not let him see you."

Tom nodded and hopped to the pond. He saw the shiny stones glittering in the water. He wanted to get one, but he was afraid of the big fish. He waited until the fish was far away, then he jumped into the pond. He grabbed a shiny stone and tried to hop out. But he was too clumsy. He slipped and splashed and made a lot of noise. The big fish heard him and turned around. He saw Tom and opened his mouth.

Tom was scared and screamed, "Help! Help! The fish is going to eat me!"

The owl heard Tom and flew to the pond. He saw the fish and said, "Stop! Do not eat Tom. He is my friend. He has a shiny stone for me. If you let him go, I will give you a magic spell too. A spell that can make you swim very fast and far."

The fish was curious and greedy. He wanted to try the magic spell. He said, "OK, owl. I will let Tom go. But you have to give me the spell first."

The owl said, "OK, fish. The spell is this: Swim, swim, swim, as fast as you can. Swim, swim, swim, to the other end of the pond. Then swim back and say, 'I am the fastest fish in the world.'"

The fish liked the sound of the spell. He said, "Swim, swim, swim, as fast as I can. Swim, swim, swim, to the other end of the pond." He let Tom go and swam away.

Tom was happy and relieved. He thanked the owl and gave him the shiny stone. The owl said, "Thank you, Tom. Now I will give you the magic spell. The spell is this: Hop, hop, hop, as high as you can. Hop, hop, hop, to the top of the hill. Then hop back and say, 'I am the best hopper in the world.'"

Tom liked the sound of the spell. He said, "Hop, hop, hop, as high as I can. Hop, hop, hop, to the top of the hill." He hopped away.

The owl smiled and watched Tom and the fish. He knew that the spells were not real. He had tricked them. He had made them practice and exercise. He had made them more confident and happy. He had helped them in his own way. He was a wise owl. He flew away with his shiny stone.

One day, Tom was sick and had to stay in bed. His mom gave him a pill to make him feel better. She said he had to swallow it with water. Tom did not like pills. They were hard and bitter. He hid the pill under his tongue and pretended to drink the water.

His mom left him alone and said she would come back later. Tom spit out the pill and put it on his nightstand. He did not want to take it. He wanted to play with Big Red. He reached for his truck, but he knocked over the pill. It rolled off the nightstand and under the bed.

Tom got out of bed and crawled under the bed to find the pill. He saw a lot of dust and some old toys, but no pill. He heard his mom coming back. He was afraid she would be angry if she saw he did not take the pill. He crawled deeper under the bed, hoping she would not see him.

"Tom, are you awake?" his mom asked. She opened the door and saw his empty bed. She saw the glass of water and the pill on the floor. She frowned. She looked under the bed and saw Tom's feet. She bent down and pulled him out. "Tom, why did you disturb the pill? You have to take it to get well. It's not a toy, you know."

Tom felt ashamed. He did not mean to disturb the pill. He just wanted to play with Big Red. He looked at his mom and said in a small voice, "I'm sorry, mom. I don't like pills. They are yucky."

His mom hugged him and said, "I know, sweetie. But they are good for you. They help you fight the germs that make you sick. How about this? If you take the pill now, I will let you play with Big Red for a little while. OK?"

Tom nodded. He took the pill and swallowed it with water. It was still hard and bitter, but he did not spit it out. He wanted to make his mom happy. He wanted to play with Big Red. He smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. Can I have Big Red now?"

His mom smiled and said, "Of course, honey. Here you go. But don't forget to rest, too. You need to sleep to get well. I love you, Tom."

She gave him Big Red and kissed him on the forehead. She left him alone and closed the door. Tom hugged Big Red and played with him on his bed. He felt a little better. He did not disturb the pill anymore. He was a good boy.

Lily and Tom felt sorry. They did not want to make the stream dirty or hurt the fish. They liked the stream and the fish.

"We are sorry, Mama," they said. "We did not know. We were just playing."

Mama smiled. She was not angry. She knew they did not mean to do bad.

"It's okay, children," she said. "But you have to be careful and respectful of nature. The stream and the fish are part of our world. We have to keep them clean and happy."

She gave them a bucket and a net. "Why don't you help me remove the stones and sticks from the stream?" she asked. "Then the water will be clean and the fish will be happy again."

Lily and Tom nodded. They took the bucket and the net and followed Mama. They worked together to remove the stones and sticks from the stream. They saw the water become clean and the fish swim freely.

They felt happy and proud. They learned to be kind and responsible. They thanked Mama for teaching them. They hugged her and said they loved her.

Mama hugged them back and said she loved them too. She was proud of them. They had learned a valuable lesson.

"Hi, I'm Lily. I live in that house," she said, pointing to her own house. She held out her bell. "Do you want to play with me?"

Lily felt sad and confused. She did not understand why the boy did not want to talk to her. She thought he was shy like her. She tried again.

The boy did not look at her. He did not listen. He did not care.

The boy covered his ears and cried. He did not like the noise. He did not like the girl. He wanted her to go away.

She wanted to say sorry, but she could not. The men grabbed her and pushed her away. They told her to go home and never bother them again. They told her she was a bad girl.

When they finished eating, they hugged each other. They were filled with joy and continued their walk through the woods.

A little boy named Jack was walking through the woods. He could hear a strange voice echoing through the forest. Jack got closer and closer, and noticed the voice was coming from a fat tree at the center of the woods. As he looked closer Jack could see the tree was shaking and its branches were waving around. He was so curious he wanted to climb it.

Jack hesitated for a moment, but then decided to make his way up the fat tree. He finally made it to the top and he saw what was making the voice. It was an old, rusty birdhouse with a strange opening in the back. Jack stuck his finger in the opening, but suddenly the birdhouse started to shake and he lost his grip. He watched as the birdhouse started to fall from the tree.

Jack was terrified, but then he heard the voice again. It was the same one he had heard before. He looked around and he was surprised to see an owl perched on top of a nearby branch. The owl was shaking its head and Jack could see it was warning him. The voice was saying: "Fall, fall!" 

Jack was so grateful to the owl. It had saved him just in time! He waved goodbye to the owl and thanked it before running back home. He would never forget the wise owl's voice.

One day, they decided to play a game. They would take turns to pick a word from the dictionary and ask the other to say what it meant. If they answered correctly, they would get a point. If they did not know, they would lose a point.

Anna picked the word "mention". She asked Ben, "What does mention mean?"

Ben thought for a moment. He remembered hearing the word before, but he was not sure. He said, "Mention means to say something quickly."

Anna smiled and said, "That is right! You get a point. Now it is your turn."

Ben picked the word "furious". He asked Anna, "What does furious mean?"

Anna frowned. She did not know the word. She tried to guess, but she was wrong. She said, "Furious means to be very happy."

Ben shook his head and said, "No, that is wrong. Furious means to be very angry. You lose a point. I win the game!"

Anna felt sad and angry. She did not like to lose. She said, "You are not fair! You picked a hard word. I do not want to play with you anymore!"

Ben smiled and said, "Yes, we can play again. But this time, let us pick easy words. And let us have fun and not worry about points. Deal?"

Anna nodded and said, "Deal!"

They hugged and picked up the dictionary. They continued to play and learn new words. They were happy and intelligent friends. 

The moral of the story is: Learning new words is fun and useful, but we should not be proud or angry when we play with others. We should be kind and forgiving, and enjoy the game.

Lily smiled. She liked to teach Max new things. She was happy that he wanted to learn.

"Hello, kids," he says. "Do you need some help?"

Tom and Mia are surprised. They did not know that. They feel sorry.

"We are sorry, sir," they say. "We did not know. We thought it was a ball. We wanted to play with it."

The man nods. He is not angry. He is kind. He picks up the fire extinguisher and puts it in his truck.

"I understand," he says. "But you should be careful. There are many things that look like toys, but they are not. They can hurt you or others. You should always ask an adult before you play with something you don't know."

Tom and Mia nod. They have learned a lesson. They thank the man.

Tom and Mia are happy. They smile. They take the ball. They say goodbye to the man.

"Goodbye, sir," they say. "Thank you for the ball. And thank you for putting out fires. You are very brave."

The man smiles. He waves. He drives away.

Bear nodded. He loved honey. He followed Bee to the hive. But when they got close, they heard a loud buzz. Many bees came out of the hive. They were angry. They did not like strangers near their home.

"Go away!" they shouted. "This is our honey. You cannot have it!"

Bear was frightened. He did not want to be stung by the bees. He ran away from the hive. But Bee stayed. He said, "Please, do not be mad. This is my friend. He is nice. He just wants to try some honey. Can you share some with him?"

The bees did not listen. They said, "No! We worked hard for this honey. We will not share it with anyone. You must leave too. Or we will sting you!"

Bee was sad. He did not want to leave his home. He did not want to lose his friend. He said, "But this is my home too. I live here with you. Why are you so mean to me?"

The bees said, "You are not one of us. You are different. You have a different color. You have a different smell. You have a different friend. You do not belong here. Go away!"

Bee felt hurt. He did not understand why the bees were so mean. He said, "But I am a bee too. I have wings. I have stripes. I have a stinger. I can make honey too. Why do you not like me?"

The bees said, "You are not a real bee. You are a fake bee. You are a bad bee. You do not follow the rules. You do not do your work. You do not help the hive. You only play with your friend. You are a lazy bee. You are a troublemaker. You are not welcome here. Go away!"

Bee was very sad. He did not know what to do. He wanted to stay in his home. He wanted to be friends with the bees. He wanted to be a good bee. But the bees did not want him. They only wanted to hurt him. They only wanted to demand their honey. They only wanted to be alone.

Bee decided to leave. He said, "Fine. I will go away. I do not need you. I do not want to be with you. You are not my friends. You are not my family. You are mean bees. You are selfish bees. You are lonely bees. Goodbye!"

Bee flew away from the hive. He looked for Bear. He found him hiding behind a bush. He said, "I am sorry, Bear. I could not get you any honey. The bees were very mean. They did not want to share. They did not want me either. They said I am not a real bee. They said I do not belong here. They said I have to go away."

For a few weeks, Frankie and the crane each settled into a comfortable routine. Every day Frankie would cheerfully greet the crane and the bird would crane its head in response. Frankie felt so safe and relaxed with his friend. 

But one day, the crane changed. Instead of waving its head, it fixed its eyes on Frankie. Frankie wasn't sure why its friend was looking at him like that, with an intense seriousness. Frankie tried to keep the feeling of joy and relaxation, but he couldn't shake the feeling that something was wrong. 

The next day, the crane flew away, leaving Frankie alone in the pond. Frankie looked around to see if his friend had left a message, thinking the crane had had to go somewhere or do something important. But there was nothing.

A tear rolled down Frankie's face. He had become so comfortable and happy with the crane that he hadn't been honest with himself about how much the bird had been taking from him. Frankie was sad and disappointed, but he realized he had a lesson to learn. Now that he was alone again, he must remember to be honest and stay vigilant.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a new goose. It was brown and had a wide neck. It looked different from the other geese. Tom and Lily wanted to pet it. They walked slowly to the brown goose. The brown goose did not run away. It looked at them with its small eyes.

Tom reached out his hand to touch the brown goose. The brown goose opened its wide mouth and bit Tom's finger. Tom cried out in pain. He pulled his hand back. The brown goose had borrowed his finger for a moment. It did not want to share.

Lily ran to Tom and hugged him. She said sorry to him. She said the brown goose was mean. She said they should go back to the other geese. The other geese were nice. They liked to eat bread and seeds.

Tom and Lily walked away from the brown goose. They did not want to play with it anymore. They went to the other geese and fed them. The other geese made happy noises. Tom and Lily smiled. They liked the other geese. They did not like the brown goose. The brown goose was bad. It liked to borrow fingers.

Anna was sick. She had a red face and a hot head. Mommy gave her a thermometer to see how sick she was. Anna did not like the thermometer. It was cold and hard in her mouth. She wanted to spit it out.

Mommy said, "No, Anna, you have to keep the thermometer in your mouth for a little while. It will tell me if you have a fever. Then I can give you some medicine to make you feel better."

Anna tried to be good. She closed her eyes and waited for the thermometer to beep. She thought about her favorite toy, a big yellow ball. She liked to play with the ball in the park. She liked to throw it and catch it and bounce it. She wished she could play with the ball now.

The thermometer beeped. Mommy took it out of Anna's mouth and looked at it. She frowned. "Oh, Anna, you have a very high fever. You need to rest and drink some water. I will get you some medicine."

Anna felt sad. She did not want to rest. She wanted to play. She saw the ball on the floor. She reached for it. She wanted to strike it with her hand and make it fly. But Mommy stopped her. She said, "No, Anna, you can't play with the ball now. You are too sick. You need to stay in bed."

Anna was angry. She did not like Mommy's words. She did not like the thermometer. She did not like the medicine. She did not like being sick. She threw the thermometer on the floor. It broke. It made a loud noise. Mommy was shocked. She said, "Anna, what did you do? That was a bad thing to do. You could have hurt yourself or me. You need to say sorry."

Anna felt sorry. She saw Mommy's face. She saw the broken thermometer. She saw the ball. She realized she had done a bad thing. She said, "Sorry, Mommy. I was mad. I don't like being sick. I want to play with the ball."

Mommy hugged her. She said, "I know, Anna. I don't like being sick either. But sometimes we have to do things we don't like to get better. I love you, Anna. I want you to be well. The medicine will help you. The ball will wait for you. When you are better, we can play with the ball together."

Anna smiled. She said, "I love you, Mommy. I want to be well too. I will take the medicine. I will rest. I will wait for the ball."

Mommy kissed her. She said, "Good girl, Anna. You are very brave. You will be better soon. I will be with you."

Anna closed her eyes. She felt warm. But not too warm. She felt Mommy's hand. She felt the ball. She felt happy. She fell asleep.

One day, a farmer went to his field to plant some seeds. He had a big bag of seeds and a shovel. He dug holes in the ground and put some seeds in each hole. He was very happy to see his field full of seeds.

But he did not see a big bird in the sky. The bird was hungry and saw the seeds. The bird flew down and started to eat the seeds. The farmer heard the bird and ran to his field. He shouted at the bird, "Go away, bird! Those are my seeds!"

The bird was scared and flew away. But it did not go far. It waited for the farmer to leave. The farmer did not leave. He stayed in his field and watched the bird. He had a plan.

He went to his barn and got a scarecrow. A scarecrow is a thing that looks like a person, but is not. It has a hat and a coat and a stick. The farmer put the scarecrow in his field. He made it look like it was holding a shovel. He hoped the bird would think it was him.

He hid behind a tree and waited. The bird came back and saw the scarecrow. It thought it was the farmer. It was not afraid. It flew down and ate more seeds. The farmer saw the bird and jumped out of his hiding place. He ran to the bird and waved his shovel. He said, "Ha! I got you, bird! You are not smart!"

The bird was surprised and tried to fly away. But it was too late. The farmer caught the bird with his shovel. He put the bird in a cage. He said, "You will not eat my seeds anymore. You will stay in this cage until the end of the day. Then I will let you go, but you will never come back."

The bird was sad and sorry. It said, "Please, farmer, let me go. I will not eat your seeds anymore. I will find other food. I will be your friend."

The farmer felt sorry for the bird. He said, "Okay, bird, I will let you go. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will not eat my seeds or any other farmer's seeds. You have to eat only worms and bugs and berries. Do you promise?"

The bird nodded and said, "I promise, farmer, I promise. Thank you for being kind to me."

The farmer opened the cage and let the bird go. The bird flew away and said, "Goodbye, farmer, goodbye. I will keep my promise. You are a good farmer."

The farmer smiled and said, "Goodbye, bird, goodbye. I hope you find enough food. You are a good bird."

The farmer went back to his field and planted more seeds. He was happy and proud. He had saved his seeds and made a new friend. He hoped his seeds would grow and give him a good harvest. He hoped the bird would be happy and healthy. He hoped they would meet again someday. The end.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers, birds and bugs. They liked to play and run on the grass.

"Look, Tom, I found a worm!" Lily said. She held a long, thin worm in her hand. It was brown and wiggly.

"Wow, let me see!" Tom said. He took the worm from Lily and looked at it. He thought it was funny and ticklish.

"Can we cook the worm?" Tom asked. He had an idea. He wanted to make a joke.

"No, Tom, we can't cook the worm. That's mean and yucky!" Lily said. She did not like Tom's idea. She wanted to put the worm back in the dirt.

"But it would be fun!" Tom said. He ran to the bench where their mom was sitting. He had a thick book in his hand. He wanted to use the book as a pan.

"Mom, look what I have!" Tom said. He showed the worm to his mom.

"Tom, what are you doing with that worm?" Mom asked. She was surprised and curious.

"I want to cook it!" Tom said. He smiled and opened the book. He put the worm on the book.

"Tom, no, don't cook the worm!" Mom said. She was shocked and worried. She took the book and the worm from Tom.

"Tom, that's not nice. The worm is alive. It needs the dirt and the air. You can't cook it. It would hurt the worm and make it die." Mom said. She explained to Tom why he should not cook the worm.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I didn't know. I just wanted to make a joke." Tom said. He felt sorry and sad.

"It's okay, Tom. I know you didn't mean to be bad. But you have to be gentle and kind to the animals. They are our friends. Do you understand?" Mom said. She hugged Tom and kissed him.

"I understand, Mom. I love you." Tom said. He hugged Mom and kissed her.

Mom took Tom and Lily to the dirt. She helped them put the worm back in the dirt. The worm was happy and safe.

"Bye, worm. Have a nice day." Tom and Lily said. They waved to the worm.

"Good job, Tom and Lily. You are good kids. Now, let's go home and have some cookies. How does that sound?" Mom said. She smiled and took their hands.

"Yay, cookies! That sounds good!" Tom and Lily said. They smiled and followed Mom.

They left the park and went home. They had a good day. They learned something new. They were happy.

But Sam did not know that the door was the door to his mom and dad's room. And his mom and dad were sleeping in their bed. And they heard the sound of his pencil on the door. And they woke up and saw his writing. And they were very angry. And they came out of their room and yelled at Sam. And they took away his paper and pencil. And they sent him to his room. And they said he could not write anymore.

Sam was troubled. He did not understand why his mom and dad were so mad. He did not mean to make them mad. He just wanted to write. He liked to write. He wrote on paper, on walls, on books, on anything he could find. He wrote his name, he wrote shapes, he wrote stories. He wrote with pens, with crayons, with markers, with paint. He wrote all the time.

Lily was a little girl who liked to display her toys. She had many toys, but her favorite was a big red nose. She liked to put it on and make funny noises. She always made her mom and dad laugh.

One day, Lily wanted to show her nose to her friend Sam. She put it in her backpack and went to his house. She knocked on the door and Sam opened it. He was happy to see her.

"Hi, Lily! Do you want to play?" he asked.

"Yes, Sam! I have something to show you. It is very funny," she said.

She opened her backpack and reached for her nose. But her hand felt nothing. Her backpack was empty. She looked inside and saw a hole. Her nose had fallen out on the way.

"Oh no! Where is my nose?" she cried.

Sam saw her sad face and hugged her. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can find your nose. Maybe it is on the street. Let's go and look."

They went outside and followed the path that Lily had taken. They looked for the big red nose. They asked people if they had seen it. But no one had.

Lily was very sad. She thought she had lost her nose forever. She said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I wanted to display my nose to you. But now it is gone."

Sam said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sure we will find it. Maybe it is at the park. We can go there and play. Maybe someone found it and left it there."

They went to the park and looked around. They saw swings and slides and benches and trees. But they did not see the nose.

They decided to play on the swings for a while. They pushed each other and had fun. They forgot about the nose for a moment.

Then, Lily heard a familiar noise. It was a honk. She looked up and saw a clown. He was wearing a big red nose. He was making balloons for the children.

Lily ran to the clown and said, "Excuse me, sir. Is that your nose?"

The clown smiled and said, "No, little girl. This is not my nose. This is your nose. I found it on the street. I thought it was a toy. I was going to give it back to you. But I saw you were sad. So I decided to wear it and make you laugh."

He took off the nose and gave it to Lily. She was very happy. She thanked the clown and hugged him. She said, "You are very kind, sir. You made me laugh. And you gave me back my nose. Thank you very much."

She put on the nose and honked it. She ran to Sam and said, "Look, Sam! I found my nose. The clown had it. He was very nice. He wanted to display it to me. He wanted to make me happy."

Sam was happy too. He said, "That's great, Lily. I'm glad you have your nose back. It is very funny. Can I try it?"

Lily said, "Sure, Sam. You can try it. We can share it. We can display it to everyone. We can make them laugh."

They took turns wearing the nose and honking it. They made the clown and the children and the parents laugh. They had a lot of fun. They learned that sometimes, losing something can lead to finding something better. They learned that displaying something can mean sharing something. They learned that laughing is the best thing to do.

He ran to his mom and told her what happened. His mom hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Your balloon is gone. It was an accident. It's okay to be sad, but don't be scared. It was just a balloon. We can get you another one."

Tom nodded and sniffed. He felt a little better. His mom said, "Why don't we go outside and play? Maybe we can see some birds or planes that soar in the sky. They are fun to watch, too."

Tom smiled and said, "Okay, mom. Let's go." He took his mom's hand and they went outside. He looked up and saw a blue sky. He saw a bird that soared high and a plane that soared low. He pointed at them and said, "Look, mom. Soar, soar, soar!"

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, Tom. Soar, soar, soar!" They played and watched the sky. Tom forgot about his balloon. He was happy.

Tom and Lily were playing near the river. They liked to splash water on each other and make boats from leaves and sticks. They saw a hut on the other side of the river. It looked old and empty.

"Let's go and see the hut," Tom said. "Maybe we can find something fun inside."

Lily was not sure. She was afraid of the river. It was deep and fast. She was also afraid of the hut. It looked dark and scary.

"No, Tom, I don't want to go," Lily said. "The river is too big and the hut is too far. We might get lost or hurt."

Tom did not listen to Lily. He was curious and brave. He made a big boat from a log and a rope. He told Lily to sit on the boat with him. He said he would be careful and they would be back soon.

Lily did not want to make Tom sad. She loved her brother. She sat on the boat with him. She held his hand. Tom pushed the boat into the river. He tried to steer it with a stick.

But the river was stronger than Tom. It carried the boat away from the hut. It made the boat spin and bump. Tom and Lily were scared. They screamed for help. They dropped the stick and the rope. They could not control the boat.

The boat hit a rock. It broke into pieces. Tom and Lily fell into the water. They were soaked and cold. They tried to swim to the shore. But the water was too deep and fast. They could not reach the shore.

They saw a man on a bridge. He heard their screams. He threw a rope to them. He pulled them out of the water. He wrapped them in a blanket. He took them to his hut. He was kind and friendly. He gave them hot soup and dry clothes. He called their mom and dad.

Tom and Lily were sorry. They learned their lesson. They thanked the man for saving them. They hugged their mom and dad. They promised to be careful and listen to each other. They never played near the river again.

They crawled and crawled. The tunnel was long and twisty. They could not see the light anymore. They could not hear the birds or the people. They only heard their own breaths.

"Ben, where are we?" Lily asked. She felt cold and wet. She wanted to go back.

"I don't know," Ben said. He tried to find a way out. He pushed and pulled the dirt. He did not find a way out. He only made the tunnel smaller.

"Ben, stop!" Lily said. "You are making it worse! We have to be patient and wait for help!"

But Ben did not listen. He was angry and scared. He kept pushing and pulling the dirt. He made the tunnel collapse. The dirt fell on them. They could not move. They could not breathe. They could not scream.

They were trapped in the tunnel. They were never found. They did not play in the park anymore.

Tim and Sue like to play with dough. They make shapes and animals and pretend they are real. One day, they find a big box of dough in the closet. They are very happy and take it to the table.

"Look, Tim, we can make a lot of things with this dough!" Sue says.

"Yes, let's make a cake and a car and a dog!" Tim says.

They open the box and take out the dough. But the dough is not soft and squishy. It is hard and rough. It does not bend or stretch. It hurts their hands.

"This is not dough, this is fake!" Sue says.

"Who put this fake dough in the box?" Tim says.

They hear a laugh from behind the door. It is their big brother, Ben. He enters the room and sees their faces.

"Ha ha, I fooled you! That is not dough, that is clay. You can't play with clay, it is for big kids. I switched the boxes when you were not looking. You are too little to play with dough, you should play with blocks or dolls." Ben says.

Tim and Sue are very angry and sad. They do not like Ben's joke. They do not like Ben. They throw the clay at him and yell.

"Go away, Ben, you are mean! We can play with dough, we are not too little. You are the one who should play with blocks or dolls. You are a big baby!" Tim and Sue say.

Ben is surprised and mad. He dodges the clay and runs out of the room. He slams the door and shouts.

"You are the babies, not me! You can't play with clay, you will make a mess. You are silly and dumb!" Ben says.

Tim and Sue do not care what Ben says. They hug each other and look for the real box of dough. They find it under the bed and take it to the table. They make a cake and a car and a dog and have fun. They are happy and smart. They like to play with dough.

Lily screamed and ran back inside. She had blood and water on her face and her coat. She cried and looked for her mom. Her mom heard her and came to help her. Her mom saw the cat and the puddle and the scratch. Her mom was mad and sad.

Her mom hugged Lily and cleaned her face. She put a bandage on the scratch and gave her a kiss. She told Lily to never splash on the porch again. She told Lily to stay away from the fat cat. She told Lily to be careful and quiet.

Lily was sorry and hurt. She did not like the fat cat or the porch or the puddle. She did not want to splash anymore. She wanted to stay inside and play with her toys. She learned a hard lesson. She had a bad day.

One day, Jen went to the park with her mom. She brought her purple ball with her. She saw a big hill and wanted to go up. She asked her mom if she could. Her mom said yes, but be careful. Jen smiled and ran to the hill with her purple ball.

Jen started to climb the hill. She held her purple ball in her hand. She liked how the hill was high and green. She liked how the sun was bright and warm. She liked how the wind was soft and cool. She was happy.

But then, something bad happened. Jen slipped on a rock and fell down. She let go of her purple ball. Her purple ball rolled down the hill. It rolled faster and faster. It rolled away from Jen. Jen was sad.

Jen got up and ran after her purple ball. She wanted to get it back. She shouted, "Stop, ball, stop!" But the ball did not stop. It rolled to the edge of the hill. It rolled over the edge. It flew in the air. Jen was scared.

Jen reached the edge of the hill. She looked down. She saw her purple ball. It was not on the ground. It was not in the air. It was in a tree. A big, tall tree. A tree with many branches and leaves. A tree that Jen could not climb. Jen was frustrated.

Jen cried. She wanted her purple ball. She missed her purple ball. She needed her purple ball. She called her mom. Her mom came and saw what happened. Her mom hugged Jen and said, "Don't worry, sweetie. We'll get your ball back. Look, there's a ladder. Maybe someone can help us."

Jen looked and saw a ladder. It was leaning on the tree. It was a long, strong ladder. It was a ladder that could reach the ball. Jen felt a little hope. She wiped her tears and said, "Please, mom, please. Can we try?"

Her mom nodded and said, "Yes, we can try. But we have to be careful. And we have to ask permission. Come on, let's go." She took Jen's hand and walked to the ladder. She saw a man. He was wearing a hat and a shirt. He had a tool and a bag. He was working on the tree. He was a tree man.

Her mom said, "Excuse me, sir. Can we talk to you for a minute?" The tree man looked at them and said, "Sure, what can I do for you?" Her mom said, "My daughter lost her ball in the tree. It's her favorite ball. It's purple. Can you please help us get it back?"

The tree man smiled and said, "Of course, I can help you. I like purple too. It's a nice color. Where is the ball?" Jen pointed and said, "There, there. It's in that branch. It's stuck. Can you see it?" The tree man looked and said, "Yes, I see it. Don't worry, I'll get it for you. Just wait here."

The tree man climbed the ladder. He went up and up. He reached the branch. He grabbed the ball. He came down and down. He gave the ball to Jen. Jen was happy. She hugged the ball and said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. You're the best. You're my hero." The tree man laughed and said, "You're welcome, you're welcome, you're welcome. I'm glad I could help. You're very sweet. You're my friend."

Jen smiled and said, "Can I give you a hug?" The tree man said, "Sure, why not?" Jen hugged the tree man and said, "You're very nice. I like you." The tree man said, "You're very nice too. I like you too." Jen's mom said, "Thank you so much, sir. You're very kind. We appreciate it." The tree man said, "It's my pleasure, ma'am. You're very welcome. Have a nice day."

Jen and her mom said goodbye to the tree man. They walked back to the hill. Jen held her purple ball in her hand. She felt it rise and fall with her breath. She felt it warm and soft with her touch. She felt it happy and safe with her love. She liked her purple ball very much.

Then they heard a voice behind them. It was a man with a funny hat and a big basket. He said, "Hi, kids! That's my balloon. I'm going for a ride in the sky. Do you want to come with me?"

Mia and Ben looked at each other. They were surprised and curious. They asked their mom if they could go. Their mom said yes, but only if they held her hand and wore a seat belt.

They also saw the balloon's shadow on the ground. It looked like a big smile. Mia and Ben realized that the balloon was waving at them after all. They felt happy and silly. They laughed and said, "Sorry, sunshine balloon! We did not see your wave. We like you too!"

The man smiled and said, "That's okay, kids. The balloon likes you too. It's just a little shy. Sometimes it gets embarrassed when people wave at it. But it's very friendly and kind. It likes to share its sunshine with everyone."

Mia and Ben nodded and said, "We understand. We sometimes get embarrassed too. But we also like to share our sunshine with everyone. Thank you for taking us for a ride, mister. You are very nice."

The man said, "You're welcome, kids. You are very nice too. And very brave. Not everyone likes to fly in a balloon. But you do. You are very special."

They hugged the man and thanked him again. Then they landed back in the park and said goodbye to the balloon. They waved at it one last time and said, "See you soon, sunshine balloon! We hope you have a good day!"

The balloon waved back and said, "See you soon, Mia and Ben! I hope you have a good day too!"

"Yes, Tom, it is!" Sam said, as he watched the boat zoom across the tub.

Lily knew just what to do. She grabbed a spoon and started to stir the honey back into the jar. Buzz watched from a flower outside and thought it was very kind of Lily to help clean up the mess. From then on, Buzz made sure to only taste the nectar from flowers and never bother any more jars of honey.

The frog jumps out of her pocket and goes back to the pond. It is happy to be free. Sue is not happy. She is sick and hurt. She needs help. But Tom is gone. He is too afraid to come back. Sue is alone and sad. The end.

Tom and Lily were two kids who liked to play in the park. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. One day, they saw a big bird in a cage near the park. The bird was very pretty, with bright feathers and a long tail. It looked sad and hungry.

"Who is this bird?" Tom asked.

"That is the king of the birds," a man said. He was the owner of the bird. "He is very rare and great. I bought him for a lot of money. But he is very shy and does not like people. He only eats special seeds that I bring him."

"Can we feed him?" Lily asked.

"No, you can't. He is mine and he does not need your food. Go away and play somewhere else," the man said. He was very rude and mean.

Tom and Lily felt sorry for the bird. They wanted to make him happy and friendly. They had some bread and nuts in their backpacks. They waited until the man was not looking and threw some food into the cage. The bird saw the food and came closer. He ate the bread and nuts and made a happy sound. He looked at Tom and Lily and smiled.

"Thank you for feeding me," the bird said. "You are very kind and brave. I don't like this cage and this man. He does not care about me. He only cares about money. He does not know that I am the king of the birds and I have a great power. I can grant you one wish each. What do you wish for?"

Tom and Lily were surprised and happy. They thought about their wishes. Tom wished for a new bike, because his old one was broken. Lily wished for a new doll, because her old one was lost. The bird nodded and said, "Your wishes are granted. But you have to do one more thing for me. You have to open this cage and let me go. I want to be free and fly with my friends. Will you do that for me?"

Tom and Lily agreed. They opened the cage and the bird flew out. He thanked them again and said, "You are the best kids I ever met. You have a good heart and a good mind. You know how to share and care. You are not greedy and selfish like the man. You deserve your wishes and more. Remember, the true king is not the one who has the most, but the one who gives the most. Goodbye and good luck!"

The bird flew away and Tom and Lily ran to their new bike and doll. They were very happy and proud. They learned a valuable lesson that day. They learned that feeding the king of the birds was better than owning him. They learned that being kind and generous was better than being rude and mean. They learned that freedom and friendship were better than money and power. They learned that the king of the birds was great, and so were they.

Lily serves the ball to Sam. Sam spikes the ball back to Lily. Lily catches the ball with her hands. She throws the ball to Ben. Ben tries to spike the ball to Mia. But he is clumsy. He slips and falls. The ball goes over his head and out of the park.

"Oops!" Ben says. He feels sad. He thinks he ruined the game.

Lily and Ben feel happy. They thank Mia and Sam. They all become friends. They decide to play volleyball again next week. They hope to have more fun and learn more skills. They also hope Ben will be less clumsy.

The bad man ran away with Ben's horn. Ben was left alone and bleeding. He was very sad and scared. He felt poor without his horn. He could not play or fight with his friends anymore. He felt ugly and weak.

The farmer heard Ben's cry and came to help him. He saw what the bad man had done and felt sorry for Ben. He wrapped a cloth around Ben's wound and gave him some water and hay. He hugged Ben and told him he was still a good goat. He said he would take care of him and protect him from the bad man.

Ben felt a little better. He thanked the farmer and licked his hand. He still missed his horn, but he was glad he had a friend. He hoped his horn would grow back someday. He learned that horns are not as important as kindness and love.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big slide that looked fun. Tim ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. Kim followed him, but she was scared. She did not like high things.

"Come on, Kim, it's easy!" Tim said. "Just sit and slide down. Whee!"

Tim slid down the slide and laughed. He waited for Kim to join him. But Kim did not move. She sat on the top of the slide and cried.

"I can't, Tim, I can't!" Kim said. "It's too high and fast. I want to go back."

Tim felt sorry for Kim. He wanted to help her. He had an idea.

"Kim, don't cry. I have a secret for you. Do you want to hear it?" Tim said.

Kim nodded. She liked secrets.

"OK, listen. The slide is not real. It's just a lie. It's made of paper and glue. It can't hurt you. It's empty inside. There's nothing there. You can slide down and nothing will happen. Trust me, Kim. It's a lie."

Kim looked at Tim. He sounded serious. He was her brother. He would not lie to her. Maybe he was right. Maybe the slide was a lie. Maybe it was empty.

"Are you sure, Tim?" Kim asked.

"Sure, I'm sure. Come on, Kim. It's a lie. It's empty. It's fun. Let's slide together." Tim said.

He held out his hand to Kim. Kim took his hand. She felt brave. She decided to trust Tim. She decided to slide.

They slid down the slide together. They felt the wind and the sun. They felt happy and free. They reached the bottom and smiled.

"That was fun, Tim!" Kim said. "Thank you for telling me the secret. The slide was a lie. It was empty. But it was fun."

Tim hugged Kim. He was proud of her. He was glad she slid. But he also felt guilty. He knew he lied to her. He knew the slide was not a lie. He knew it was not empty. He knew it was real. He knew he lied to make her slide. He wondered if she would ever find out. He wondered if she would ever forgive him. He wondered if he did the right thing. He wondered what life would be like if he told the truth.

One day, a little boy was playing in the forest with his friends. He saw a big stone that looked shiny and pretty. He wanted to take it home and show his mom. He ran to the stone and tried to lift it, but it was too heavy. He dropped it on his foot and cried out loud.

His friends came to help him. They saw his foot was bleeding and hurting. They did not know what to do. They looked around and saw an old man sitting under a tree. He had a long beard and kind eyes. He looked wise and gentle.

They ran to the old man and asked him for help. The old man smiled and said, "Don't worry, my children. I have something that can heal your friend's foot. It is a special plant that grows in this forest. It has green leaves and yellow flowers. It can make the pain go away and the wound heal faster. Follow me and I will show you where to find it."

The old man led them to a clearing where the plant was growing. He picked some leaves and flowers and crushed them in his hand. He squeezed the juice on the boy's foot and wrapped it with a cloth. He said, "There, that should feel better. Now, let me tell you a story about this plant and this stone."

The old man told them that the plant and the stone were once friends. They lived together in harmony and shared their gifts. The plant gave the stone its beauty and the stone gave the plant its strength. But one day, the stone became greedy and wanted more beauty. He took all the plant's flowers and left it with only leaves. The plant became sad and angry. He cursed the stone and made it lose its shine and become dull and rough.

The old man said, "The plant and the stone learned a hard lesson. They realized that they were better off when they were friends and shared their gifts. They apologized to each other and became friends again. The plant gave back some of the flowers and the stone gave back some of the shine. They healed their friendship and their hearts."

The old man said, "The moral of the story is that greed and selfishness can hurt yourself and others. Friendship and generosity can heal and make you happy. Remember this, my children, and always be kind and fair to your friends and to nature."

The children thanked the old man for his help and his story. They hugged the boy and said they were sorry for his foot. They said they would always be his friends and share their toys and snacks. They took the stone and gave it to the old man as a gift. They said it was a symbol of their friendship and gratitude. The old man smiled and said he was proud of them. He said he would keep the stone and remember them. He said goodbye and wished them well.

The children went back to their homes, feeling happy and wise. They learned a valuable lesson that day. They learned that friendship can heal.

Sam and Tom were friends who liked to play with fire. They found a box of matches in the kitchen and took it to the backyard. They lit some leaves and sticks and watched the fire grow. They thought it was funny to see the smoke and the sparks.

"Look, Sam, the fire is so big and bright!" Tom said.

"Yes, Tom, it is fun to make fire!" Sam said.

But they did not see that the fire was spreading to the fence and the shed. The fire caught some paint cans and made a loud boom. The fire also reached the trash bin and made a bad smell. The fire was not funny anymore. It was scary and dangerous.

"Help, help, fire!" Sam and Tom shouted.

Their mom and dad heard them and ran to the backyard. They saw the fire and called the firemen. The firemen came with a big truck and a hose. They sprayed water on the fire and put it out. They also checked if Sam and Tom were hurt. They were not hurt, but they were very scared and sorry.

"Sam, Tom, what did you do?" their mom and dad asked.

"We played with matches and made fire," Sam and Tom said.

"Do you know how dangerous that is? You could have burned the house or yourselves! You could have hurt someone else! You are very lucky that the firemen came in time!" their mom and dad said.

Sam and Tom looked at the backyard. It was black and gray. There was ash everywhere. The fence and the shed were burned. The paint cans and the trash bin were melted. The leaves and the sticks were gone. The backyard was not pretty anymore. It was ugly and sad.

"Sam, Tom, do you see what you did? Do you see how much damage you caused?" their mom and dad said.

"Yes, mom, yes, dad, we see," Sam and Tom said.

"Do you regret playing with fire?" their mom and dad said.

"Yes, mom, yes, dad, we regret playing with fire," Sam and Tom said.

"Playing with fire is not a game. It is not funny. It is very bad and wrong. You should never do it again. You should always listen to us and be careful. Do you understand?" their mom and dad said.

"Yes, mom, yes, dad, we understand," Sam and Tom said.

Sam and Tom hugged their mom and dad and said they were sorry. Their mom and dad hugged them back and said they loved them. They also said they had to clean the backyard and fix the fence and the shed. They also said they had to learn from their mistake and be good and smart. Sam and Tom nodded and said they would.

The end.

Moral value: Playing with fire is dangerous and wrong. You should listen to your parents and be careful. You should learn from your mistakes and be good and smart.

Her mom said, "The drain is very deep and you might get hurt."

Lily said, "Okay, I will be careful. Can I jump in it just one time?"

Her mom thought for a moment and said, "Okay, but only one time. And remember to count to three before you jump, so I know you are being safe."

Lily counted, "One, two, three!" and jumped in the puddle. It splashed water everywhere and the light from the sun made the water sparkle. Lily was very happy and said, "That was fun! Can I do it again?"

Her mom laughed and said, "Okay, just one more time." And Lily counted again, "One, two, three!" and jumped in the puddle again.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with pens and paper. They draw many things, like stars, flowers, and animals. They have fun and share their pens.

One day, Tom finds a new pen. It is very shiny and pretty. It has many colors. Tom likes the shiny pen a lot. He does not want to share it with Lily. He hides it in his pocket.

Lily comes to play with Tom. She sees his paper. It has many shiny colors. She asks Tom, "Can I see your pen? It is very pretty."

Tom says, "No, it is my pen. You cannot have it. Go away."

Lily feels sad. She says, "But we are friends. We always share our pens. Why are you mean to me?"

Tom says, "I don't care. This is my pen. I don't need you."

Lily cries and leaves. Tom feels happy. He thinks he has the best pen in the world. He draws more things with his shiny pen.

But soon, Tom feels lonely. He has no one to play with. He has no one to talk to. He has no one to show his drawings to. He looks at his shiny pen. It does not make him happy anymore. He misses Lily. He wishes he had shared his pen with her.

He runs to find Lily. He sees her playing with other friends. They are drawing with their pens and paper. They are smiling and laughing. They look healthy and happy.

Tom feels sorry. He says to Lily, "Lily, I am sorry. I was wrong. I was selfish. I should have shared my pen with you. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends again?"

Lily looks at Tom. She sees his shiny pen. She sees his sad face. She says, "Tom, I forgive you. You are my friend. You can play with us. You can share your pen with us. We can share our pens with you."

Tom feels happy. He gives his shiny pen to Lily. He says, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. You are a good friend. I like your pens too. They are very nice."

Lily smiles. She says, "You are welcome, Tom. You are a good friend too. I like your pen too. It is very shiny."

They hug and play with their pens and paper. They draw many things, like stars, flowers, and animals. They have fun and share their pens.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Being selfish makes you lonely. Being kind makes you happy.

The story foreshadows or sets up the conflict by introducing the man with the mean face and the big net at the end of the first paragraph. It pays off or resolves the conflict by revealing his plan and motive at the end of the last paragraph. The story also creates suspense and curiosity by making the reader wonder what will happen to the puppy and the children.

Tom and Anna felt sorry. They realized that they were wrong. They hugged mom and Ben. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We are sorry, Ben. We love you. We will not shut the door and lock it again. We will be nice to you. We will play with you and share our toys and our dog."

Mom smiled and kissed them. She said, "I am glad you learned your lesson. I love you all. Now let's go to the kitchen and have some cookies and milk."

The moral of the story is: You should love and respect your family, especially the ones who are smaller and weaker than you. You should not shut them out or ignore them. You should help them and make them happy.

Ben and Mia were hungry. They wanted to eat waffles for breakfast. Mom said they could make waffles with the waffle maker. She showed them how to pour the batter and close the lid.

Ben and Mia waited for the waffle maker to beep. They smelled the yummy waffles. They wanted to eat them right away. But Mom said they had to yield. Yield means to wait and let someone else go first.

"Who will get the first waffle?" Mom asked.

"Me!" Ben said.

"Me!" Mia said.

They both reached for the waffle. They pulled and tugged. The waffle broke in half. Ben and Mia were sad. They looked at the broken waffle. They looked at Mom. They were confused.

"Why did you break the waffle?" Mom asked.

"We both wanted it!" Ben said.

"We didn't want to yield!" Mia said.

Mom sighed. She said, "Yielding is not bad. It is good. It means you are kind and fair. It means you share and care. It makes everyone happy. Do you want to be happy?"

Ben and Mia nodded. They said, "Yes, we want to be happy."

Mom smiled. She said, "Then let's make another waffle. And this time, you can take turns. Ben, you can get the first half. Mia, you can get the second half. And then you can swap and try each other's waffles. How does that sound?"

Ben and Mia liked that idea. They said, "That sounds good!"

They made another waffle. They yielded. They shared. They cared. They ate the waffles. They were happy. Mom was happy too. She said, "You are good kids. I love you."

Ben and Mia hugged Mom. They said, "We love you too, Mom. And we love waffles!"

"Who took my axe? Who did this?" he shouted.

"Let's have a race!" he said.

The three of them each took one post and started running, giggling as they went. Little Johnny, the 3 year old, was having a lot of fun, but he didn't always do what Daddy said.

"You need to put your post there to be fair Johnny," said Daddy. 

But Johnny didn't want to move his post. He yelled "NO!" and started to cry. 

Momma put her arm around Johnny and said "It's not good to not listen to Daddy. If we all do what he said, it's fair and we can have a good time". 

So Johnny moved his post and they all raced to the end. Everyone had fun and it was a good day in the park. 

The moral of this story is that it's important to listen to your parents and do the right thing for everyone to have a good time.

But then, she ran out of space. She wanted to draw Ben's body, arms, and legs. But there was no more room on the paper. She was sad. She did not know what to do. She did not want to waste her paper. She did not want to start over.

She thought hard. She had an idea. She decided to stretch her paper. She took some tape and scissors. She cut the paper in half. She taped the two pieces together. She made the paper longer. She was smart.

She finished her picture. She drew Ben's body, arms, and legs. She added some details, like his shirt, pants, and shoes. She wrote his name and "my hero" on the paper. She was proud.

She showed her picture to Ben. He was surprised and happy. He hugged her and thanked her. He said he liked her picture very much. He said she was very creative and clever. He said she was his hero too. They smiled.

The moral of the story is: You can use your creativity to solve problems and make something beautiful. You can also show your love and appreciation to your hero.

"Okay, pepper. You can play with me. You can tell me where the pieces go. We can do it together. We can be friends," she said.

The pepper smiled. It was happy. It thanked Lily. They started to do the puzzle together. They had fun. They were friends. They both won.

One day, a mole was digging in the ground. He liked to make tunnels and find food. He was very hungry, so he dug deeper and deeper. He did not see the trap that a farmer had set for him.

The trap was a big metal thing with sharp teeth. When the mole touched it, it snapped shut and hurt him a lot. He tried to get out, but he could not. He felt very scared and sad.

A mouse came by and saw the mole in the trap. He felt sorry for him and wanted to help. He said, "Hello, mole. I am a mouse. You are in a trap. It is very bad. Do you want me to offer you some cheese? Maybe it will make you feel better."

The mole looked at the mouse and said, "Thank you, mouse. You are very kind. But I do not want cheese. I want to be free. Can you open the trap for me?"

The mouse said, "I will try, mole. But it is very hard. The trap is very strong. I have to be careful not to get hurt too."

The mouse tried to open the trap with his teeth and his paws. He pulled and pushed and bit and scratched. But he could not open it. He got tired and sore. He said, "I am sorry, mole. I cannot open the trap. It is too hard for me. Maybe someone else can help you."

The mole said, "It is okay, mouse. You did your best. You are a good friend. But I think I will not make it. I feel very weak and cold. I think I will die soon."

The mouse said, "No, mole. Do not say that. Do not give up. Maybe someone will come and save you. Maybe the farmer will change his mind and let you go. Maybe a big bird will come and break the trap. Do not lose hope, mole."

The mole said, "Thank you, mouse. But I do not think so. I think this is the end for me. Goodbye, mouse. I hope you have a good life. I hope you find a lot of cheese and a nice home. I hope you are happy."

The mouse said, "Goodbye, mole. I will miss you. You are a brave and nice mole. I hope you find peace and rest. I hope you are happy too."

The mole closed his eyes and stopped breathing. He was dead. The mouse cried and said, "I am sorry, mole. I wish I could have helped you. I wish you were still alive. You are my friend."

The farmer came and saw the mole in the trap. He was happy and said, "Ha! I got you, you pesky mole. You will not dig in my land anymore. You will not eat my crops anymore. You will not bother me anymore. You are dead."

He took the mole out of the trap and threw him away. He did not see the mouse. He did not care about the mole. He did not know that the mole had a friend. He did not know that the mole had a story. He did not know that the mole had a life. He was a bad farmer.

Lily knew she had to help the bee. She carefully untangled the bee from the web and set it free. The bee flew away happily and Lily felt proud of herself for helping. From that day on, Lily wasn't scared of bees anymore and she knew that sometimes it's important to ask for help when you need it. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing hide and seek. Lily found a hiding spot behind a big tree. She waited there for a long time until it started to get dark. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and felt scared. She started to shiver and felt very cold.

Lily looked up and saw a big, angry dog. She didn't know what to do, so she closed her eyes and imagined a happy image in her head. She thought of her mom's warm hugs and her dad's silly jokes. Suddenly, she remembered that her dad had told her to stay still and quiet if she ever saw a scary dog. So, Lily stayed very still and quiet. The dog sniffed around for a little while and then walked away.

Lily was so relieved and happy that she had remembered what her dad had told her. She ran back to her friends and told them all about her scary adventure. They were all amazed and proud of her for being so brave. From that day on, Lily knew that she could handle anything as long as she stayed calm and remembered what her parents had taught her.

Lila and Ben were playing in the backyard. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for shiny things. Sometimes they found rocks, sometimes they found coins, sometimes they found nothing.

"Look, look, I found something!" Ben shouted. He held up a round, brown thing in his hand. It was a little bit shiny, but not very much.

"What is it?" Lila asked. She ran over to see.

"I don't know. Maybe it's a penny. Maybe it's a button. Maybe it's a treasure!" Ben said. He rubbed the thing with his fingers, but it did not get any shinier.

Lila took the thing from Ben and looked at it closely. She saw some letters and numbers on it. She could not read them, but she knew they were letters and numbers. She also saw a picture of a man with a hat.

"Ben, this is not a penny or a button or a treasure. This is a copper. It's a kind of money from a long time ago. My dad told me about it. He has some in a box. He said they are very old and very rare," Lila said.

"Wow, really? How do you know?" Ben asked.

"Because I saw them. And because they look like this. See, they have the same letters and numbers and the same man with a hat. And they are brown and not very shiny. That's how you know they are copper," Lila said.

Ben realized that Lila was right. He had never seen a copper before. He felt very lucky and very happy. He hugged Lila and thanked her for telling him.

"Can we keep it? Can we show it to your dad?" Ben asked.

"Sure, we can keep it. And we can show it to my dad. Maybe he will tell us more about it. Maybe he will let us see his box of coppers. Maybe he will give us one. He is very nice and very smart," Lila said.

They put the copper in their pocket and ran inside. They were very excited and very curious. They were also very persistent. They did not stop asking Lila's dad about the copper until he agreed to show them his box and tell them a story. They learned a lot and had a lot of fun. The next day, Timmy brought his dad's keys and tried to unlock the door again. This time, he succeeded! He went inside and saw lots of cool machines and experiments. But then, he heard footsteps coming towards him. It was the lab owner! 

Timmy was scared, but the lab owner was nice and showed him around. Timmy learned a lot about science that day and was happy he unlocked the door. From then on, he always asked before entering a lab.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally loved candy, but her mommy said she could only have it on Tuesdays. Sally didn't like that rule, but she followed it anyway.

One Tuesday, Sally's mommy gave her a big bag of candy. Sally was so happy! She ate all the candy and didn't save any for later. But then, Sally started to feel sick. Her tummy hurt and she didn't feel good. 

The next Tuesday, Sally's mommy offered her some candy, but Sally refused. She remembered how she felt when she ate too much candy last time. Sally learned her lesson and didn't want to feel spoiled again. From then on, Sally only ate a little bit of candy on Tuesdays and felt much better.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to jump around and play all day long. One day, Timmy's parent took him to the park to play. Timmy was so excited to jump on the big, bouncy castle.

As Timmy was jumping, he accidentally bumped into another kid. The kid's parent got embarrassed and said, "Watch where you're going!" Timmy's parent quickly apologized and said, "I'm sorry, Timmy didn't mean to bump into your child."

Timmy's parent then asked him, "Are you okay, Timmy?" Timmy replied, "Yes, I'm okay. Can I keep jumping?" His parent smiled and said, "Of course, just be careful and watch where you're going." Timmy happily continued to jump and play, enjoying his day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to cook with her mom. One day, they were making pancakes for breakfast. Lily's job was to find the pan. She looked high and low, but she couldn't find it anywhere.

"Lily, did you find the pan?" asked her mom.

"No, I can't find it," replied Lily.

Suddenly, Lily's little brother came into the kitchen. He had taken the pan to play with his toys. When he saw the pancakes, he wanted to help. He poured syrup all over them, making them extra sweet.

But when they all sat down to eat, they realized the pan was ruined. It was melted from being on the stove for too long. Lily's mom was very upset. "Now we can't make pancakes anymore," she said. Lily felt sad that she couldn't help her mom make breakfast anymore.

Suddenly, it started to rain! Lily's mom said, "We have to go home now or we will get wet." But Lily said, "Wait, I have an idea!" She took out a unique umbrella that she had brought and said, "Let's use this to stay dry!" 

Everyone thought it was a great idea and they had a fun picnic under the umbrella. They ate their sandwiches and played games until the rain stopped. Lily was proud of herself for coming up with such a good idea.

Once upon a time, there was a red bird. The red bird lived in a tree. One day, the red bird saw a big onion on the ground. The red bird said, "I want to eat the onion, but it is too big for me to eat alone."

Just then, a green frog hopped by. The red bird said, "Hello green frog, will you help me eat this big onion?" The green frog said, "Sure! But first, let's fight to see who gets the biggest piece."

So the red bird and the green frog had a little fight. The red bird won and got the biggest piece of onion. They both ate the onion and were happy. From that day on, they became good friends and shared everything they found. The end.

Suddenly, Lily noticed a brick on the ground. She asked, "Mommy, what is that brick for?" Mommy explained, "We use bricks to make a path in the garden. It helps us walk without stepping on the flowers." 

Lily tried to pick up the brick, but it was too tight. She said, "Mommy, the brick is too heavy for me. Can you help me?" Mommy smiled and said, "Of course, I'll help you. Together, we can make a beautiful garden with pretty flowers and a nice path."

Tim and Lily were playing on the beach with their sand toys. They liked to make castles and tunnels and moats. They saw a big boat on the water. It was white and shiny and had a flag.

"Look, Lily, a yacht!" Tim said, pointing at the boat.

"What is a yacht?" Lily asked.

"A yacht is a big boat that people use to have fun and travel. It is very nice and expensive," Tim explained.

"I want to go on a yacht," Lily said.

"Me too, but we can't. We don't know anyone who has a yacht. And we need to ask our parents first," Tim said.

"Maybe we can make a fake yacht with sand," Lily suggested.

"OK, let's try," Tim agreed.

They worked hard to shape a big pile of sand into a boat. They used sticks and shells and seaweed to decorate it. They made a flag with a piece of cloth and a twig. They pretended to steer and sail and wave at other boats.

They had so much fun that they forgot about the time. Their parents came to look for them and saw their sand yacht.

"Wow, what a great yacht you made!" their mom said.

"Thank you, mom. It is our fake yacht. We can't go on a real one," Lily said.

"Well, you have a lot of imagination and creativity. But now it is time to go home and bathe. You are very sandy and salty," their dad said.

"OK, dad. Can we come back tomorrow and play with our yacht again?" Tim asked.

"Sure, if the tide doesn't wash it away. But remember to wear sunscreen and drink water. The sun is very hot," their mom said.

They packed their sand toys and followed their parents to the car. They waved goodbye to their fake yacht and hoped to see it again. They were happy and tired from their beach day.

"Tom, why are you frowning?" Sara asked. "Don't you want to go on a journey?"

"No, I don't," Tom said. "I want to stay home and play. I don't like journeys. They are long and boring."

"But journeys are fun," Sara said. "You can see new places and meet new people. And you can play with me and mom and dad. We can sing songs and tell stories and play games in the car."

Tom shook his head. He did not want to sing or tell stories or play games. He wanted to play with his toys and his friends. He crossed his arms and looked out the window.

The car drove for a long time. Sara saw many things. She saw cows and horses and sheep. She saw trees and flowers and hills. She saw houses and shops and signs. She pointed and asked mom and dad what they were. Mom and dad told her and she learned new words.

Tom did not see anything. He closed his eyes and pretended to sleep. He did not want to learn new words. He knew enough words already.
