Tom walked slowly behind mom and dad. He did not want to meet his aunt and his cousins. He did not want to share his room and his toys. He did not want to make new friends.

Sara smiled and said hello. She followed her aunt into the house. She wondered what the surprise was.

Tom frowned and said nothing. He followed mom and dad into the house. He did not care about the surprise. He wanted to go home.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were explorers. They saw a big hill with a hole on top. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's go and see!" Tom said. "Maybe it is a volcano!"

"A volcano?" Lily asked. "What is that?"

"A volcano is a mountain that makes fire and rocks. It is very loud and hot. But we are brave, we can go and look!" Tom said.

They climbed the hill and reached the hole. They peeked inside. They saw nothing but dirt and rocks.

"Is this a volcano?" Lily asked.

Tom shook his head. "No, this is not a volcano. This is just a hole. I guess we were wrong."

They heard a noise behind them. They turned around and saw a man with a big hose. He was watering the flowers.

"Hello, kids. What are you doing here?" the man asked.

"We were looking for a volcano!" Tom said.

"A volcano? In the park?" the man laughed. "There are no volcanoes here. Volcanoes are far away, in other places. Do you want to learn more about them?"

"Yes, please!" Tom and Lily said.

The man smiled and took them to his truck. He had a book and a toy volcano. He showed them pictures and told them stories. He also made the toy volcano erupt with water and baking soda.

Tom and Lily were amazed. They learned a lot about volcanoes. They thanked the man and went back to their parents.

They decided to play something else. They still liked to pretend they were explorers, but they also liked to learn new things. They wondered what else they could find in the park.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy trains on the floor. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving fast. Ben had a red train and Lily had a blue one.

"Look, my train has steam!" Ben said, blowing on his train. He saw some white air come out of the train's chimney. "It can go very far with steam."

Lily tried to blow on her train, but nothing happened. She blew harder and harder, but still no steam. She felt frustrated. Why did Ben's train have steam and hers did not?

"Ben, why does your train have steam and mine does not?" Lily asked, frowning.

Ben looked at Lily's train. He saw that it was different from his. His train had a hole on the top, but Lily's train did not.

"Your train is not the same as mine, Lily," Ben said. "Your train does not have a hole for the steam. It is a different kind of train."

Lily looked at her train. She saw that Ben was right. Her train did not have a hole for the steam. It had a button instead.

"What does this button do?" Lily asked, pointing at the button.

Ben shrugged. He did not know. He had never seen a train like Lily's before.

"Why don't you try it?" Ben said. "Maybe it will do something fun."

Lily nodded. She pressed the button. Suddenly, her train made a loud sound and flashed a bright light. It was a siren!

"Wow!" Ben and Lily said together. They laughed and clapped their hands. They liked the siren.

"Your train is cool, Lily," Ben said. "It can make a siren. That is fun."

"Thank you, Ben," Lily said. "Your train is cool too. It can make steam. That is fun."

Ben and Lily smiled at each other. They decided to share their trains and play together. They did not feel frustrated anymore. They felt happy. They reminded each other that different trains can do different things, and that is okay.

"Hey, you two," Jake said. "Do you want to see something cool in the bathroom?"

He ran away and left Tom and Lily alone. They saw the water on the floor and the toilet still overflowing. They were scared and wet.

"Help, help!" Tom and Lily cried. "Let us out, Jake! Let us out!"

But Jake did not hear them. He was hiding in his room. He was not nice. He was mean.

Tom and Lily hugged each other and cried. They wished they were still playing with their toys in the living room. They were not happy. They were sad.

The end.

Sam and Lily were friends who liked to play near the water. They saw a big boat with white sails and many windows. It was a yacht. They wanted to go on the yacht and see what was inside.

They waited until no one was looking and climbed on the yacht. They saw many things they did not understand. There were buttons and screens and wires and maps. They touched some of the buttons and heard noises and saw lights. They thought it was fun.

But they did not know that they were making the yacht move. The yacht started to go away from the shore and into the deep water. They did not see the rocks and the waves. They did not hear the people shouting and waving. They did not feel the yacht shaking and tipping.

Soon they were scared and wanted to go back. But they did not know how to stop the yacht or turn it around. They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had listened to their parents and stayed away from the yacht.

A big boat with a red light and a loud horn came to help them. It was a rescue boat. The people on the rescue boat were kind and brave. They threw a rope to the yacht and pulled it back to the shore. They helped Sam and Lily get off the yacht and gave them blankets and hugs.

Sam and Lily said they were sorry and thanked the people on the rescue boat. They learned a great lesson. They learned that they should not go on things they do not understand. But it didn't work. The monster was too strong and Lily was too scared. The monster took Lily and her book and disappeared into the night. Lily's parents never saw her again.

One day, a little dragon came to the castle. The king and queen were surprised and happy to see the dragon. They welcomed the dragon to the party and had a great time. The little dragon became friends with all the people at the party and they all had fun together. From that day on, the little dragon was always welcome at the castle.

The little girl was amazed and asked, "Can I ride in the truck?" The driver said, "Sorry, but it's not safe for little girls to ride in big trucks. But you can watch it go down the road and see how it starts and moves with all its power." 

The little girl watched the truck go down the road and saw how it started and moved with all its power. She was very happy to see the big truck and thanked the driver for showing her. The end.

On the way home, they saw a big loop in the road. Timmy thought it looked like a fun slide so he asked Max if he wanted to go down it with him. Max barked happily and they ran over to the loop. Timmy climbed up and Max followed him.

When they got to the top, Timmy was so excited that he forgot to be scared. They slid down the loop together and it was so much fun that they did it again and again. Timmy was no longer shivering and he knew he was lucky to have such a great friend like Max.

His mom shook her head. "No, Sam, you can't open this letter. This letter is not for us. It is for Mr. Lee. He is waiting for this letter. It is very important to him. We have to be good and dependable neighbors. We have to respect his mail. Do you understand?"

Sam nodded. He understood. He did not want to make Mr. Lee sad or angry. He wanted to be a good and dependable neighbor. He said, "Okay, mom, I won't open this letter. Can I help you give it to Mr. Lee?"

His mom smiled. "Yes, Sam, you can help me give it to Mr. Lee. That is very nice of you. Come on, let's go. Maybe he will permit us to have a cookie with him." She took Sam's hand and they walked to Mr. Lee's house. Sam held the letter carefully. He was happy to help his mom and Mr. Lee. He liked to be a good and dependable neighbor.

Tim and Sam like to play cricket in the park. They have a bat, a ball and two sticks. They take turns to hit the ball and run. They count how many runs they make.

One day, a nosy dog comes to the park. He sees the ball and wants to play too. He runs after the ball and catches it in his mouth. He does not give it back to Tim and Sam. He runs away with the ball.

"Hey, that is our ball!" Tim shouts. "Give it back, dog!"

Sam runs after the dog. He tries to get the ball from him. But the dog is fast and clever. He dodges Sam and runs to the other side of the park.

Tim and Sam are sad. They cannot play cricket without the ball. They sit on the grass and wait for the dog to come back.

The dog has fun with the ball. He chews it and throws it in the air. He thinks he is the best at cricket. He thinks he can win against anyone.

But then he sees another dog. A bigger dog. A dog with a loud bark. The bigger dog wants the ball too. He runs towards the nosy dog and growls.

The nosy dog is scared. He drops the ball and runs away. He does not want to play cricket anymore. He wants to hide.

The bigger dog picks up the ball and brings it to Tim and Sam. He wags his tail and licks their faces. He is a friendly dog. He wants to share the ball.

"Thank you, dog!" Tim says. "You are a good dog!"

Sam smiles. He takes the ball and throws it to Tim. They start to play cricket again. They have fun with the friendly dog. They forget about the nosy dog.

They think they are the best at cricket. They think they can win against anyone.

Sara was a shy girl who liked to play with her dolls in her room. She did not like loud noises or big crowds. She was happy when her mom gave her a potato for lunch. She liked to eat potatoes because they were soft and yummy.

One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Tom and he liked to play with cars and trucks. He was not shy at all. He liked to make loud noises and talk to everyone. He saw Sara playing with her dolls in her room and he wanted to join her.

He knocked on her door and said, "Hi, I'm Tom. Can I play with you?"

Sara was scared and hid behind her bed. She did not want to play with Tom. She did not know him and he was too loud. She said, "No, go away. You disturb me."

Tom was sad and confused. He did not understand why Sara did not want to play with him. He liked to play with everyone. He said, "But I just want to be your friend. Why are you so shy?"

Sara did not answer. She hugged her potato and her dolls. She wished Tom would leave her alone.

Tom did not give up. He thought of a way to make Sara like him. He went to his kitchen and got a potato. He carved a face on it and made it look like a doll. He put a ribbon on it and gave it a name. He called it Patty.

He knocked on Sara's door again and said, "Look, I have a potato doll too. Her name is Patty. Can she play with your dolls?"

Sara nodded and said, "Yes, it's nice. But be careful with the knife. It can hurt you."

Tom said, "Don't worry, I was careful. Can I come in and play with you?"

Sara thought for a moment. She was still shy, but she was also lonely. She liked potatoes and dolls. Maybe Tom was not so bad after all. Maybe he could be her friend. She said, "Okay, you can come in. But don't be too loud. You disturb me."

Tom said, "Okay, I'll be quiet. Thank you for letting me play with you."

Tom climbs the hill. It is hard and steep and long. He gets tired and sweaty and thirsty. But he does not give up. He wants to see the view. He reaches the top and looks around. He sees the farm, the cows, the plants, the eggs. He sees the road, the cars, the people, the shops. He sees the sky, the sun, the clouds, the birds. He sees a lot of things he has never seen before. He is amazed and happy.

Tom stays on the hill for a while. He enjoys the view. He feels proud of himself. He did a good work. He is strong and fast and happy. He decides to go back to the farm. He runs down the hill. He sees his dad waiting for him. His dad smiles and hugs him. He tells him he is proud of him too. He asks him what he saw. Tom tells him everything. They go back to the farm together. They are strong and fast and happy.

Lily and Max were twins who loved to explore. One day, they found a strange machine in their dad's workshop. It had a big button that said "shrink".

"What does this do?" Lily asked.

"Let's find out!" Max said. He pushed the button and pointed the machine at Lily.

Zap! Lily felt a tickle and then she was very small. She was as big as a bug.

"Max, look what you did!" Lily shouted. But Max could not hear her. She was too tiny.

Max saw Lily disappear and got scared. He looked around and saw her on the floor.

"Lily, are you okay?" he said. He bent down to pick her up.

"Max, don't touch me! You might hurt me!" Lily said. She ran away from his hand.

She saw a mouse hole and ran inside. She hoped to find a safe place.

Max followed her. He pushed the button again and pointed the machine at himself.

Zap! He felt a tickle and then he was very small too. He was as big as Lily.

"Lily, where are you?" he called.

"I'm here, Max. Come inside!" Lily said. She saw Max enter the mouse hole.

They hugged each other and felt better.

"Sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to shrink you," Max said.

"It's okay, Max. But how do we get big again?" Lily said.

They looked at the machine. It was far away and too big for them to carry.

They decided to look for help. They went on a tour of the mouse hole. They saw many things. They saw cheese and crumbs. They saw a nest and a ball. They saw a spider and a fly. They saw a cat and a dog.

They were careful and intelligent. They avoided the spider and the fly. They hid from the cat and the dog. They made friends with the mouse. The mouse was nice and helped them.

He took them to the machine and pushed the button. He pointed the machine at Lily and Max.

Zap! They felt a tickle and then they were big again. They were as big as before.

They thanked the mouse and said goodbye. They took the machine and ran to their dad.

"Dad, dad, look what we found!" they said.

They showed him the machine and told him their story.

Dad was surprised and proud. He hugged them and said:

"You are very brave and curious, Lily and Max. But please, don't play with my shrink machine again. It's not a toy. It's for my work."

Lily and Max nodded and smiled. They learned a lot from their adventure. They never forgot their tour of the mouse hole.

Lily and Ben were twins who loved to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big truck that made loud noises and moved by itself. They called it Zoomy.

One day, they were playing with Zoomy in the living room, when they heard their mom call them for lunch. "Lily, Ben, come and eat your soup!" mom said. But Lily and Ben did not want to stop playing. They ignored mom and kept zooming Zoomy around the couch.

Mom came to the living room and saw them. She was not happy. "Lily, Ben, I told you to come and eat your soup. Why did you not listen to me?" she asked. Lily and Ben looked at mom and felt sorry. They knew they had been bad.

"We are sorry, mom. We love Zoomy too much. Can we play with him after lunch?" Lily said. Ben nodded. Mom sighed. She loved her twins, but they had to learn to obey.

"Okay, you can play with Zoomy after lunch, but only if you eat your soup and say sorry to me. And you have to share Zoomy with each other. If you fight over him, I will punish you. Do you understand?" mom said. Lily and Ben nodded. They hugged mom and said sorry. They followed mom to the kitchen and ate their soup.

After lunch, they went back to the living room and played with Zoomy again. They took turns to zoom him around and made him say funny things. "Zoomy is the best toy ever. He is so fast and loud and adorable. He makes us happy." Lily said. Ben agreed. They smiled and laughed and had fun. Mom watched them from the kitchen and smiled too. She was glad they had made up and learned their lesson. She thought they were adorable too.

Sara likes to dress up in her red swimsuit. She has a big pool in her backyard. She wants to swim with her friends. She puts on her swimsuit and runs outside.

But when she gets to the pool, she sees something scary. There is a big frog in the water. It is green and slimy. It croaks loudly. Sara is afraid of the frog. She does not want to swim with it.

She runs back to the house. She tells her mom about the frog. Her mom smiles and says, "Don't worry, Sara. The frog is not bad. He just wants to cool off in the pool. He will not hurt you. He is your friend."

Sara is not sure. She looks at the frog again. He looks at her and winks. He jumps out of the pool and hops away. Sara sees that he is not so scary. He is just a frog.

She decides to give him a chance. She says, "Bye, frog. Maybe we can swim together next time." She jumps into the pool and splashes with her friends. She is happy. She likes her red swimsuit and her big pool. And she likes the frog, too.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They lived in a big house near a valley. The valley had many trees and flowers and animals. Sometimes, Anna and Ben would go to the valley with their mom and dad and have a picnic.

One day, Anna and Ben wanted to play a game in the valley. They decided to play repeat. Repeat was a game where one of them would say something and the other would say the same thing. They thought it was funny to hear their voices echo in the valley.

Anna went first. She said, "Hello, hello, hello!" Ben repeated, "Hello, hello, hello!" They heard their voices bounce back from the hills. They laughed and clapped their hands.

Then Ben said, "I like cake, I like cake, I like cake!" Anna repeated, "I like cake, I like cake, I like cake!" They heard their voices echo again. They smiled and rubbed their tummies.

But then Anna said something that Ben did not like. She said, "Ben is silly, Ben is silly, Ben is silly!" Ben did not repeat. He felt angry and sad. He did not think it was funny to call him silly. He said, "Stop it, stop it, stop it!"

Anna did not stop. She repeated, "Ben is silly, Ben is silly, Ben is silly!" She thought it was a joke. She did not see that Ben was unhappy. She heard her voice echo louder and louder.

Ben did not want to play anymore. He felt uncomfortable and hurt. He ran away from Anna and hid behind a tree. He cried and cried. He wished Anna would be nice to him.

Anna did not know where Ben went. She looked around and called his name. She did not hear him answer. She did not hear his voice echo. She felt scared and lonely. She wished Ben would come back to her.

Mom and Dad heard Anna and Ben. They came to the valley and found them. They hugged them and asked them what happened. Anna and Ben told them about the game and the words. Mom and Dad explained to them that words can be fun or hurtful. They told them to be careful and kind with their words. They told them to say sorry and hug each other.

Anna and Ben felt sorry and hugged each other. They said they loved each other and did not want to be mean. They promised to play nicely and not repeat bad words. They felt happy and warm again. They thanked Mom and Dad and went back to the picnic. They ate cake and sang songs. They enjoyed the valley and their voices. They repeated, "We are friends, we are friends, we are friends!"

Lily was a little girl who liked to play dress-up. She had many hats and scarves and shoes in her closet. One day, she found a big mirror in the attic. She was very happy. She wanted to see how she looked in different outfits.

She put on a red hat and a blue scarf and some yellow shoes. She stepped in front of the mirror and smiled. She thought she looked very pretty. She said, "Hello, mirror. Do you like my hat and scarf and shoes?"

The mirror did not say anything. It only showed Lily's reflection. But Lily did not know that. She thought the mirror was shy. She said, "Don't be shy, mirror. You can talk to me. I am your friend."

Then she heard a voice from behind the mirror. It was a mean voice. It said, "You are not pretty. You are ugly. Your hat and scarf and shoes are ugly. You look like a clown."

Lily was very scared and sad. She did not know who was talking. She thought the mirror was mean. She said, "No, mirror. You are wrong. You are mean. You are not my friend."

She ran away from the mirror and down the stairs. She cried and cried. She wanted her mommy.

Her mommy heard her cry and came to hug her. She asked her what was wrong. Lily told her about the mirror and the mean voice. Her mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. The mirror was not talking to you. It was a bad boy who was hiding behind the mirror. He wanted to scare you and make you feel bad. He was ugly, not you. You are beautiful and sweet and smart. I love you."

Lily felt better. She hugged her mommy and said, "I love you too, mommy. Thank you for making me feel better. Can we throw away the mirror?"

Her mommy said, "Yes, we can. We don't need a mirror to tell us how we look. We only need to look into our hearts and see how we feel. And we feel happy and loved."

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big tree with red cherries on it. They wanted to eat some cherries, but the tree was too high for them to reach.

They saw an old ladder leaning against the wall. The ladder was rusty and broken, but they did not care. They decided to take the ladder and put it against the tree. They climbed up the ladder, one by one, and picked some cherries.

"Yum, these cherries are sweet and juicy!" Tom said.

"Let's take more, there are so many!" Sam said.

They filled their pockets and mouths with cherries, and did not notice that the ladder was shaking and cracking. They did not hear the old man who owned the tree shouting at them.

"Hey, you naughty boys, get down from my tree! That's my ladder, and my cherries! You are stealing from me!" the old man said.

But Tom and Sam did not listen. They kept taking cherries, until the ladder broke and they fell to the ground. They hurt their legs and arms, and dropped all their cherries. The old man came and scolded them.

"You should be ashamed of yourselves! You took what was not yours, and you broke my ladder! You could have asked me nicely, and I would have given you some cherries. But now, you have to pay for the ladder, and you get no cherries!" the old man said.

Tom and Sam felt sorry and scared. They said they were sorry, and they ran back to their home. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that taking things without asking is wrong, and that being greedy can lead to trouble. They learned to respect other people's things, and to be thankful for what they have.

One day, a pirate named Jack was sailing on his big boat with his loyal crew. They liked to find treasure and have fun. But they also had a problem. Another pirate named Tom wanted to take their boat and treasure. He had a bigger boat and more crew. He was very mean and greedy.

Jack and his crew saw Tom's boat coming closer. They were scared and angry. They did not want to lose their boat and treasure. They wanted to fight back. But how could they win against Tom?

Jack had an idea. He saw another boat nearby. It was a boat of friendly fishers. They had nets and hooks and fish. Jack waved at them and shouted, "Help us, please! Tom is a bad pirate. He wants to take our boat and treasure. We need your help to stop him. We will share our treasure with you. We can be friends!"

The fishers heard Jack and saw Tom's boat. They did not like Tom either. He had stolen their fish before. They wanted to help Jack and his crew. They nodded and smiled. They sailed closer to Jack's boat. They used their nets and hooks to catch Tom's crew. They threw fish at Tom's boat to make it slippery and smelly.

Jack and his crew cheered and thanked the fishers. They fought together against Tom and his crew. They were brave and smart. They united to stop Tom. They made Tom and his crew surrender and go away. They saved their boat and treasure.

Jack and his crew shared their treasure with the fishers. They gave them gold and jewels and pearls. The fishers gave them fish and nets and hooks. They were happy and grateful. They became friends. They sailed away together. They were loyal and united. They were good pirates.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden. But they are not allowed to go near the big shed. The big shed has steel tools and machines. Mom and Dad say they are dangerous.

One day, Anna and Ben are bored. They see the big shed. They want to see what is inside. They are naughty. They sneak to the shed when Mom and Dad are not looking. They open the door and go in.

The shed is dark and noisy. There are many things they do not know. They see a big red button. Ben wants to press it. Anna says no. Ben says yes. He presses the button.

The machine makes a loud sound. It shakes and sparks. Anna and Ben are scared. They run out of the shed. Mom and Dad hear the sound. They come to the garden. They see the shed. They see Anna and Ben.

Mom and Dad are angry. They ask Anna and Ben what they did. Anna and Ben are sorry. They nod. They tell the truth. They say they were naughty. They say they pressed the button.

Mom and Dad are glad they are safe. But they are still angry. They say they have to fix the machine. They say Anna and Ben have to go to their room. They say they have to think about what they did. They say they have to be good. Anna and Ben nod. They go to their room. They think about what they did. They say they will not be naughty again.

Lila was a little girl who loved to fly. She had a big red kite that she took to the park every day. She ran and ran with the kite until it flew high in the sky. She felt happy when she saw the kite dance in the wind.

One day, Lila met a boy named Ben at the park. He had a blue kite that he wanted to fly too. He said hello to Lila and asked if he could fly his kite with her. Lila nodded and smiled. They ran and ran with their kites until they flew next to each other. They felt happy when they saw the kites play in the sky.

But then, a big gust of wind came and blew the kites away. Lila and Ben tried to catch them, but they were too fast. The kites flew over the trees and the houses and the cars. Lila and Ben ran after them, but they could not see them anymore. They felt sad when they lost their kites.

They ran and ran until they came to a big building. It had a sign that said "Hospital". They saw a man in a white coat who was holding a big machine. He said hello to Lila and Ben and asked what they were doing. Lila and Ben told him that they were looking for their kites. The man said that he was a doctor and that he had a machine that could see inside things. He said that it was called an x-ray. He asked if they wanted to see how it worked. Lila and Ben nodded and followed him.

The doctor took them to a room where there was a big screen and a table. He said that he had a patient who was deaf and that he wanted to see if he could help him. He said that he would use the x-ray to see his ears. He asked Lila and Ben if they wanted to see too. Lila and Ben nodded and watched. The doctor put a big hat on the patient's head and turned on the machine. The screen showed a picture of the patient's ears. The doctor pointed to a small bone that was broken. He said that it was the reason why the patient could not hear. He said that he would try to fix it with a small tool. He asked Lila and Ben if they wanted to see too. Lila and Ben nodded and watched.

The doctor used the tool to fix the bone. He said that it was done and that he would test the patient's hearing. He asked the patient to say his name. The patient said his name. He asked the patient to say what he heard. The patient said that he heard the doctor's voice. He asked the patient to say what he felt. The patient said that he felt happy. The doctor said that he was happy too. He said that the x-ray helped him to help the patient. He said that he hoped that Lila and Ben would find their kites. He said goodbye to them and thanked them for watching.

Lila and Ben said goodbye to the doctor and the patient and thanked them for showing them the x-ray. They left the hospital and went back to the park. They looked for their kites, but they could not find them. They felt sad when they thought that they would never see them again.

But then, they saw something in the sky. It was their kites. They had flown back to the park. They were still dancing in the wind. Lila and Ben ran to them and caught them. They felt happy when they held their kites. They flew them again and again until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to each other and promised to fly their kites together again. They felt happy when they made a new friend.

Ben and Lily were playing with a big puzzle. It had many pieces with different colors and shapes. They wanted to make a picture of a farm with animals and trees.

"Look, I found the cow!" Lily said, holding a piece with black and white spots. "Where does it go?"

Ben looked at the puzzle board. He saw a green piece with grass and a red piece with a barn. He pointed to a spot next to the barn. "It goes here, Lily. See, the cow lives near the barn."

Lily nodded and put the piece in the right place. She smiled and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. You support me."

Ben smiled back and said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are a good sister. You help me too."

They continued to work on the puzzle, finding more pieces and matching them. They found the horse, the pig, the sheep, the chicken, the dog, the cat, the tractor, the fence, and the farmer. They filled the puzzle board with the farm picture.

When they finished, they clapped their hands and cheered. They were very proud of their puzzle. They showed it to their mom, who was watching them from the couch.

Tommy was a chubby boy who liked to eat a lot of cake. He had a big birthday party with his friends and got many presents. He was very happy and wanted to share his cake with everyone.

But there was a problem. His uncle Bob was a lawyer who came to the party. He was very mean and greedy. He did not like to share anything. He wanted to have all the cake for himself. He took a big plate and put many slices of cake on it. He did not leave any cake for Tommy and his friends.

Tommy was very sad and angry. He wanted to have some cake too. He said to his uncle Bob, "That is not fair. You have too much cake. You have to share with me and my friends. It is my birthday."

But uncle Bob did not listen. He said, "No, this is my cake. I am a lawyer. I know the law. The law says I can have as much cake as I want. You have to do what I say. Go away, chubby boy."

Tommy did not like what his uncle Bob said. He felt very bad. He wanted to cry. But then he had an idea. He saw a big window near the table. He ran to the window and opened it. He grabbed the plate with the cake and threw it out of the window. The cake flew in the air and landed on the street. Many birds and dogs came and ate the cake.

Uncle Bob was very shocked and angry. He yelled, "What did you do, chubby boy? You wasted my cake. You are very naughty. You have to pay for this."

But Tommy did not care. He smiled and said, "No, this is your cake. You are a lawyer. You know the law. The law says you can have as much cake as you want. But you have to close the window first."

"Let's go to the cave!" Ben said.

"OK, but be careful!" Lily said.

They ran to the hill and crawled into the hole. It was dark and cold. They saw some rocks and some bugs. They heard some noises.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe a bear!" Ben said.

They were scared. They wanted to go back.

"Let's jump out of the cave!" Lily said.

"OK, but how?" Ben said.

They looked for a way out. They saw a small opening with some light. They had to jump very high to reach it.

"Can you do it?" Ben asked.

"I can try!" Lily said.

She jumped as hard as she could. She grabbed the edge of the opening. She pulled herself up.

"I did it!" Lily said.

"Good job!" Ben said.

He jumped too. He also grabbed the edge. He pulled himself up.

"We did it!" Ben said.

They were happy. They ran back to the park. They told their mom and dad about their adventure.

"Wow, you are very brave!" Mom said.

"And very smart!" Dad said.

They hugged Ben and Lily. They gave them some juice and cookies. Ben and Lily smiled. They liked the cave, but they liked their mom and dad more.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a dog. The dog is big and brown. His name is Rex.

One day, they see a high tree in the park. It has red and yellow leaves. Lily and Ben want to climb the tree. They think it is fun. They leave the ball and the dog on the ground.

But Rex does not like to stay on the ground. He likes to run and jump. He sees the ball and he wants to play. He starts to chase the ball. He runs fast and far. He does not hear Lily and Ben call him.

Lily and Ben are scared. They do not see Rex. They do not see the ball. They think Rex is lost. They climb down the tree. They look for Rex. They shout his name.

They hear a bark. They see Rex. He is not lost. He is in another part of the park. He has the ball in his mouth. He is happy. He sees Lily and Ben. He runs to them. He wags his tail.

Lily and Ben are happy too. They hug Rex. They take the ball. They say sorry to Rex. They say they will not leave him alone. They play with him and the ball. They have fun. They love Rex. Rex loves them.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. Sara wants to go first. She climbs up the ladder and sits on the slide.

"Are you ready?" she asks Tom.

"Yes, I am ready!" Tom says.

Sara slides down very fast. She is happy. She laughs and says, "Whee!"

But then she sees something on the ground. It is a pepper. A red pepper. Sara does not like peppers. She thinks they are hot and yucky. She tries to avoid the pepper, but she cannot. She slides right over it. She feels a sting on her leg. She cries out, "Ow!"

Tom slides down after her. He sees Sara crying. He is worried. He runs to her and asks, "What happened? Are you okay?"

Sara points to the pepper and says, "I hit the pepper. It hurt me. It is not nice."

Tom picks up the pepper and throws it away. He says, "I am sorry, Sara. The pepper is gone now. It will not hurt you anymore."

He hugs Sara and says, "You are brave. You are my friend. I will make you feel better."

He takes Sara to the bench. He gives her a band-aid for her leg. He gives her a cookie from his backpack. He gives her a smile.

Sara stops crying. She says, "Thank you, Tom. You are nice. You are my friend. You make me feel better."

They eat the cookie together. They share a laugh. They go back to play. They have fun. They are happy.

Lily liked to play in the garden. She liked to smell the flowers, chase the butterflies and dig in the dirt. She had a little shovel and a bucket that she used to make mud pies.

One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, you can't play in the garden today. It is too wet and cold. You will get sick and dirty. You can play inside with your toys."

Lily was sad. She did not want to play inside. She wanted to play in the garden. She said, "But mom, I love the garden. Please, can I play in the garden?"

"No, Lily, you can't. I'm sorry, but it is not safe. Maybe tomorrow, if the sun comes out, you can play in the garden. Now, come inside and have some milk and cookies."

Lily did not listen. She was angry and stubborn. She ran out of the door and into the garden. She did not care if it was wet and cold. She wanted to have fun.

But soon, Lily realized that playing in the garden was not fun at all. The flowers were droopy, the butterflies were gone and the dirt was sticky. She slipped and fell in a puddle. She got mud all over her clothes and hair. She started to shiver and sneeze. She felt miserable.

She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had played inside. She wished she had some milk and cookies. She cried and cried.

Her mom heard her cry and came out to the garden. She saw Lily in the puddle, covered in mud. She felt sorry for her. She said, "Oh, Lily, what have you done? You are wet and dirty and sick. You did not obey me. You did not allow me to help you. Come on, let's go inside and get you cleaned up."

She picked up Lily and carried her inside. She gave her a warm bath, a dry dress and a cozy blanket. She gave her some milk and cookies and a hug. She said, "Lily, I love you. I only want what is best for you. Next time, please listen to me. I know what is good for you."

Lily felt ashamed and sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you too. You are right. I should have listened to you. I should have allowed you to help me. Thank you for taking care of me. Can I play in the garden tomorrow?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, you can play in the garden tomorrow. If the sun comes out and the garden is dry and bright. But only if you promise to be careful and follow my rules."

Lily nodded and said, "I promise, mom. I will be careful and follow your rules. I will be a good girl."

Mom kissed her and said, "That's my Lily. Now, let's read a story and have a nap. You need to rest and get well."

Lily snuggled with her mom and said, "OK, mom. I like stories and naps. I like you and the garden. I am happy."

The end.

"Lily, what have you done?" she asked. "You are so careless! You have to wash up right now or you will not get any dinner!"

Lily did not want to miss dinner. She liked to eat. She followed her mother inside and went to the bathroom. Her mother turned on the water and gave her a soap and a towel.

"Scrub, scrub, scrub!" her mother said. "You have to wash all the mud off. It is dirty and bad for you."

Lily did not like to scrub. It hurt her skin and made her eyes sting. She cried and complained.

"I don't want to wash, I want to play!" she said. "Washing is boring and hard!"

Her mother did not listen. She helped Lily wash her hands and face and hair. She rinsed off the soap and dried her with the towel.

"There, now you are clean and pretty," her mother said. "But you have to be more careful next time. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She did not want to make her mother angry again. She said she was sorry and gave her a hug.

"I love you, mommy," she said.

"I love you too, Lily," her mother said. "Now let's go have dinner."

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big stick that looked like a sword. They both wanted to have it, but they did not want to share.

"I saw it first!" Lily said. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Max said. "I am stronger!"

They started to pull the stick from each other, but it was very hard. They did not notice that a dog was watching them from behind a tree. The dog liked sticks too, and he wanted to have some fun.

The dog ran towards Lily and Max and barked loudly. He jumped on them and snatched the stick from their hands. He ran away with it, wagging his tail.

Lily and Max were very surprised and scared. They let go of the stick and fell on the ground. They looked at each other and felt very silly. They realized that they had been selfish and rude. They had not listened to each other or tried to take turns. They had not enjoyed the stick at all, and now they had lost it.

They got up and hugged each other. They said they were sorry and that they loved each other. They decided to play something else together, something that did not need a stick. They learned that sharing is better than fighting, and that being kind is more fun than being selfish.

The dog watched them from a distance and smiled. He had taught them a lesson, and he had a new toy. He was happy. He did not feel embarrassed, because he did not know what that word meant. He just liked sticks.

Lila and Ben liked to play on the beach. They liked to gather shells and rocks and make shapes in the sand. One day, they saw a big sail on the water. It was white and shiny and had a flag with a star on it.

"Wow, look at that sail!" Lila said. "It must belong to a wealthy person. Maybe they have a lot of toys and candy on their boat."

"Maybe they do," Ben said. "Do you think they would share with us?"

Lila and Ben decided to wave at the sail and shout hello. They hoped the wealthy person would see them and come to the shore. They waited and waited, but the sail did not come closer. It went farther and farther away, until it was a tiny dot on the horizon.

Lila and Ben felt sad and disappointed. They wondered why the wealthy person did not want to be their friend. They went back to their shells and rocks and tried to have fun, but they were not as happy as before.

The next day, Lila and Ben went to the beach again. They were surprised to see a lot of people and cars and trucks there. They saw some men wearing uniforms and badges and carrying big guns. They also saw some men wearing masks and handcuffs and looking scared.

"What is going on?" Lila asked.

One of the uniformed men heard her and came over. He smiled and knelt down to their level.

"Hello, kids. Do you remember the sail you saw yesterday?" he asked.

Lila and Ben nodded.

"Well, that sail belonged to a very bad person. He was not wealthy, he was a thief. He stole a lot of money and jewels from a bank and tried to escape on his boat. But we caught him and his friends. We followed them on our own boat and radioed for help. Now they are going to jail and we are going to return the money and jewels to the bank."

Lila and Ben gasped. They could not believe it. The sail they admired was a sail of a criminal. They felt glad that the bad person was caught and that the good people were safe.

"Wow, you are very brave and smart," Lila said.

"Thank you," the uniformed man said. "You are very kind and curious. Do you want to see the money and jewels we found on the boat?"

Lila and Ben nodded eagerly. The uniformed man led them to a truck where there were many bags and boxes full of shiny things. He opened one of them and showed them some gold coins and sparkling necklaces.

"Look at these," he said. "They are very pretty, but they are not as important as being honest and good. Remember that, kids. Money and jewels can make you happy for a while, but they can also make you greedy and mean. The best things in life are not things, they are friends and family and love."

Lila and Ben smiled and hugged the uniformed man. They thanked him for showing them the money and jewels and for teaching them a lesson. They realized that they did not need to be wealthy to be happy. They had each other and they had fun. They went back to their shells and rocks and made shapes in the sand. They were happy again.

One day, a new boy came to her class. His name was Sam and he had curly hair and big eyes. He sat next to Lily and smiled at her. Lily felt nervous and looked down at her notebook.

"Hi, I'm Sam. What are you drawing?" he asked.

Lily did not answer. She held her notebook close to her chest and hoped he would go away.

"Can I see your notebook? I like to draw too. Maybe we can draw together," he said.

Lily shook her head. She did not want to share her notebook with anyone, especially a stranger.

Sam did not give up. He took out his own notebook and showed it to Lily. It had many pictures of animals and cars and stars. He pointed to a picture of a lion and said, "This is my favorite. I want to be a lion when I grow up. What do you want to be?"

Lily looked at his notebook and felt curious. She liked his pictures. They were bright and fun. She peeked at her own notebook and saw a picture of a flower. She wanted to be a flower when she grew up. A flower that could grow anywhere and make people happy.

She looked at Sam and saw that he was still smiling. He did not seem mean or scary. He seemed nice and friendly. Maybe he would not laugh at her or take her notebook away. Maybe he would like her pictures and her dreams.

She took a deep breath and opened her notebook. She showed him her picture of a flower and said, "This is my favorite. I want to be a flower when I grow up."

They drew flowers together in their notebooks. They talked and laughed and became friends. Lily was not shy anymore. She had someone who liked her and her notebook. She had someone who could lead her to new adventures.

She asked her mommy bee, "Can I go get nectar from that flower by myself?" Her mommy bee smiled and said, "Yes, my little bee. You can be independent now. But remember to come back to us." The little bee was so happy and flew to the flower. She got the nectar and came back to her mommy bee. 

From that day on, the little bee was more confident and independent. She still stayed with her group, but now she knew she could fly alone too.

At the store, Lily found the sweet pink ink and was so happy. She couldn't wait to go home and draw more pictures. When they got home, Lily showed her daddy all the pictures she drew with her sweet pink ink. Her daddy said, "Wow, Lily! Your pictures are so beautiful!" 

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Daddy. I love my sweet pink ink."

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had long hair that she loved to comb every day. One day, she lost her comb and couldn't find it anywhere. She looked under the bed, in the closet, and even in the toy box, but it was nowhere to be found. 

Lily's mom suggested that they guess where the comb might be. Lily thought hard and remembered that she had used it to comb her doll's hair earlier. They went to her room and there it was, hiding under the doll's blanket. 

Lily was so happy to have found her comb that she smiled brightly. She combed her hair and her doll's hair too, and they both looked beautiful. From that day on, she made sure to always put her comb in the same place so she wouldn't lose it again.

Once upon a time there was a tired ostrich. He was walking around the field looking for something to eat.

The ostrich had no choice but to obey the man's demands. He worked all day in the hot sun and he was so tired. As the sun began to set, the man told the ostrich that he could finally go home.

Marianna waved goodbye to the old man and went on her own way. She was very proud of herself that she had helped the man find his way back home.

When the bird was done, the old man was very pleased. He kept thanking the bird and said that he would show it to his family. But suddenly, the old man grabbed the harmless little bird and ate it for his dinner. The old man had tricked the poor little bird. 

The story ends sadly, and the old man's family are left brokenhearted over the bird's untimely demise.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny who wanted to fly. He thought of the idea one day while he was hopping on the ground. He wanted to soar like the birds that flew high up in the sky. "If only I had wings", he said, as he looked up to the sky.

One day, he decided to try something. He searched and searched until he found a fake pair of wings in the forest. He quickly put them on and started hopping on the ground with all his might.

"I'm flying! I'm really flying!" he shouted.

But he was wrong. No matter how high he hopped, he did not lift off the ground. Suddenly, a wise old rabbit hopped over to him.

The man nodded and said, "If you kneel and believe, magic things can happen." The boy did and suddenly he felt very dependable. The man nodded and said, "The universe is yours to explore. Just remember to be brave and trust in yourself." 

The boy thanked the man and flew away into the stars. From then on, he visited many planets, stars, and galaxies. He explored the universe and was always brave, dependable, and hopeful.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old and very polite. Jane wanted to learn how to add numbers. Her dad said he would teach her. He explained that adding meant putting two numbers together.

The first test was to add one plus one. Jane counted out two fingers. Dad smiled and said "That's right, two". Jane was very happy that she had gotten the right answer.

Next Dad said Jane should add two plus two. She counted out four fingers. Dad said "Well done, that's four!" Jane was so pleased with herself.

Dad and Jane kept adding numbers. By the end of the day Jane was very tired, but she was also very proud. She had learnt how to add and was very happy.

Lucy stepped closer and stared in wonder at the huge snowman. His top hat was big and his eyes were twinkling. He smiled at Lucy and she smiled back. 

Lucy stepped away and laughed. She had made a new friend and had a wonderful day out.

John was delighted and tried to climb up the pile. But it was slippery with steam. Suddenly, John heard a loud noise coming from inside the pile. Suddenly, a giant monster appeared. The monster was smashing rocks and trees and wanted to destroy the railway!

John got scared, but he was brave. He tried to think of a plan to stop the monster destroying the railway. He shouted and waved his arms but the monster was too big. Suddenly, he noticed the steam. "That's it!" He thought.

John used the steam to push the monster away. The monster grumbled in anger and ran away. He had saved the railway and all the trees and rocks! Everyone was so proud of John's bravery. From then on, John was known as a hero!

He stayed in the boat for hours until the sun set. Just then, he heard a loud noise. He peeked his head out of the boat and he saw a big wave coming towards him. He quickly jumped out of the boat and ran back to the shore.

The wave was so big that it lifted the boat and carried it away. But the boy was safe. He watched as the boat sailed away into the horizon. The water was so clear he could see every ripple of the wave. He was happy that he was safe.

He went back to the shore every day but the boat never returned. It didn't matter because he knew he was always safe at the shore. He would rock back and forth and smile, happy that his favorite spot was always the shore.

But Jessica got a bit too excited and started to mix the flowers carelessly. She ended up with a big blurppy mess, with daisies and buttercups all mixed together! Jessica was worried about her lawn. But, she knew what she needed to do to make it better.

Jessica carefully picked out each flower, one by one until she was done. After all the flowers were back in their original spots, the lawn looked just like new. Jessica was so proud, she ran inside to show her parents. 

From then on, Jessica was extra careful when she was mixing things on the lawn. She remembered the lesson she learned and always took extra care when she was tinkering around.

The end.

The rabbit felt so scared that he started to yell. He yelled, "No more horns! Please stop!" But the furry ape only kept making more and more noise.

Finally, the furry ape decided to take a break. He put away his horn and the animals in the forest felt relieved. The furry ape realized he should have listened to the rabbit and been quieter. From now on, he promised to play with the horn very carefully.

The toys set up a race in the living room. The razor scooter and the toy car raced around the room, laughing and having fun. The other toys cheered them on. When the rain stopped, they all went outside to play. The toys were happy to have a new friend in the razor scooter.

Tom's mom told him that he was going to be punished for not listening. Tom was sad. He didn't want to be punished. But he knew that he should have listened to his mom. Now, Tom couldn't play his guitar for a whole week. That made Tom very sad.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big meeting. All the animals were going to meet a new friend. The new friend was a big, green frog named Freddy. Everyone was very excited to meet Freddy.

Before the meeting, the little red bird told her friends, "I heard that Freddy can scream very loud." The other animals did not believe her. They thought, "How can a small frog scream so loud?"

The day of the meeting came. All the animals gathered around to meet Freddy. They all said "hello" and Freddy said "hello" back. Then, the little red bird asked Freddy, "Can you really scream very loud?" Freddy smiled and said, "Yes, I can."

All the animals looked at each other, not sure if they should believe him. Then, Freddy took a deep breath and screamed so loud that all the animals jumped in surprise. They all laughed and clapped for Freddy. The little red bird was right, Freddy could scream very loud. From that day on, Freddy and the other animals became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big, white dog named Fluffy. Fluffy had thick fur that kept him warm when it was cold outside. Fluffy loved to play outside with his friends, the birds, and the squirrels. One day, Fluffy saw a small, red thing on the ground. He did not know what it was, but he thought it looked fun to play with.

Fluffy picked up the red thing with his mouth and took it to his owner, a little girl named Sally. Sally saw the red thing and said, "Fluffy, this is a record! We can play music with it!" Sally took the record inside the house and put it on a big, round thing. The big, round thing started to spin and make music. Fluffy was very happy to hear the music and started to dance.

As the music played, Fluffy's thick, white fur began to shed. It fell like snow all around the house. Sally laughed and said, "Fluffy, you are making it snow inside!" They danced and played in the "snow" until the music stopped. Then, Sally picked up the record and put it away, so they could play with it again another day. Fluffy and Sally knew they would always remember the fun day they made it snow inside the house.

One day, a modest duck went to the pond to swim and play. He liked the water and the sun, but he did not like to show off or brag. He was happy with his feathers and his quack, and he did not want to bother anyone.

But there was another duck at the pond, who was not modest at all. He was loud and rude, and he always wanted to be the best. He had shiny feathers and a loud quack, and he liked to make fun of the other ducks.

"Look at me, I am the fastest duck in the pond!" he said. "No one can catch me or beat me. You are all slow and boring. Especially you, modest duck. You are so plain and dull. Why don't you run away and hide?"

The modest duck felt sad and hurt by the mean duck's words. He did not want to fight or argue, but he also did not want to run away. He wanted to stand up for himself and his friends.

So he said, "I may not be the fastest duck, but I am not afraid of you. You are not the best, you are just the meanest. You should be nice and kind, not loud and rude. Why don't you run away and learn some manners?"

The mean duck was surprised and angry by the modest duck's words. He did not like to be challenged or told what to do. He wanted to show the modest duck who was the boss.

So he said, "How dare you talk to me like that, modest duck? You are so weak and silly. I will show you who is the boss. I will chase you and bite you and make you run away."

And he ran towards the modest duck, with his wings flapping and his beak snapping.

But the modest duck was not weak or silly. He was brave and smart. He knew the pond and the plants and the rocks. He knew how to swim and dodge and hide.

And he ran away from the mean duck, with his feet splashing and his quack laughing.

He ran behind a reed, and the mean duck missed him. He ran under a lily, and the mean duck lost him. He ran around a rock, and the mean duck crashed into it.

The mean duck was tired and sore and confused. He could not catch or beat the modest duck. He realized he was not the fastest or the best. He was just the meanest and the worst.

He felt ashamed and sorry for his words and actions. He wished he could be nice and kind, like the modest duck.

So he said, "I am sorry, modest duck. You are not plain and dull. You are brave and smart. You are a good duck and a good friend. Can you forgive me and teach me how to be modest?"

The modest duck heard the mean duck's words. He saw the mean duck's face. He felt the mean duck's change.

And he said, "I forgive you, mean duck. You are not weak and silly. You are strong and honest. You can be a good duck and a good friend. I can teach you how to be modest."

And he ran towards the mean duck, with his wings open and his quack friendly.

And they ran together to the pond, to swim and play and learn. They became friends and shared their feathers and their quacks. They were happy and modest, and they did not bother anyone.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the park with his mom. He saw a big monkey on a tree. He wanted to play with the monkey, so he jogged to the tree and said, "Hello, monkey! Can I be your friend?"

The monkey looked at Tom and said, "No, you can't. You are too small and slow. I only play with big and fast animals. Go away, little boy!"

Tom felt sad and hurt. He jogged back to his mom and told her what the monkey said. His mom hugged him and said, "Don't listen to the monkey, Tom. He is not nice. He is rude and mean. You are a good boy, and you can make many friends who are kind and fun. Size and speed don't matter. What matters is your heart and your smile."

Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You are right. I don't need the monkey. I have you and other friends who love me."

Just then, he saw a girl his age playing with a ball. He jogged to her and said, "Hello, I'm Tom. Can I play with you?"

The girl smiled and said, "Sure, I'm Anna. I like your shirt. It has a star on it."

Tom and Anna played with the ball and had a lot of fun. They became friends and shared their snacks. The monkey watched them from the tree and felt lonely and jealous. He wished he had been nicer to Tom and learned to share and care.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge others by their appearance. Be kind and friendly to everyone. You never know who might become your friend.

The man looked at Sara's passport and smiled. He said, "You have a very pretty name, Sara. Do you know how to whistle?" Sara nodded. She loved to whistle. She could whistle songs and sounds and even her name. She opened her mouth and whistled loudly.

But then, something funny happened. When Sara whistled, her passport flew out of her hand. It went up in the air and landed on the floor. Sara was very surprised. She did not mean to do that. She felt very embarrassed.

She ran to pick up her passport. She said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to whistle my passport away." The man laughed. He said, "It's okay, Sara. It was an accident. You have a very strong whistle. Here, let me help you." He gave Sara her passport back. He said, "Have a nice trip, Sara. And keep whistling. It's a good skill to have."

Sara smiled. She said, "Thank you, sir. I will keep whistling. But not at my passport." She held her passport tightly. She walked with Ben and Mom and Dad to the plane. She was still a little embarrassed, but she was also happy. She was going on a big trip. And she had a very strong whistle.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom and dad. One day, they see a big fire truck with red lights and loud sounds. They want to go and see the fire truck.

"Can we go, mom? Can we go, dad?" they ask.

"OK, but be careful and stay close to us," mom and dad say.

They run to the fire truck and notice the firemen. The firemen are wearing helmets and coats and boots. They have hoses and ladders and axes. They look busy and brave.

"Wow, look at them!" Anna says.

"They are so cool!" Ben says.

They watch the firemen go into a house that has smoke coming out of it. They hear a siren and see another fire truck coming. They wonder what is happening inside the house.

"Is there a fire? Is someone in trouble?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. I hope they are OK," Ben says.

They wait and wait. They start to feel tired and hungry. They look for mom and dad, but they don't see them. They feel scared and alone.

"Where are mom and dad?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. Maybe they went to get us something to eat," Ben says.

They look around and see a lot of people and cars and noise. They don't know where to go. They wish they had stayed close to mom and dad.

"Anna, Ben, where are you?" they hear mom and dad call.

They turn and see mom and dad running towards them. They feel happy and relieved. They hug mom and dad and say sorry.

"We're sorry, mom and dad. We got lost. We wanted to see the fire truck," they say.

"It's OK, we're glad you're safe. But you have to listen to us and stay close to us. There are dangers in the park. You could get hurt or lost or worse," mom and dad say.

"We understand, mom and dad. We will listen to you and stay close to you. We love you," they say.

They walk back to their car and go home. They learn a lesson. They learn to obey their parents and be careful in the park. They also learn to respect the firemen and their work. They thank the firemen for saving the house and the people. They say goodbye to the fire truck and the park. They go to bed and dream of fire trucks and firemen. They are happy and safe.

One day, they want to make a big castle. They start to put blocks together. But they disagree on how to do it. Tom wants to use only yellow blocks. He says yellow is the best color. Mia wants to use all the colors. She says the castle will be more pretty.

"Yellow, yellow, yellow!" Tom says. He takes all the yellow blocks and puts them in a pile.

"No, no, no!" Mia says. She takes some yellow blocks and mixes them with other colors. She makes a wide wall.

"Stop it!" Tom says. He is angry. He pushes Mia's wall and it falls down.

"Hey!" Mia says. She is sad. She pushes Tom's pile and it scatters.

They both cry. They are not friends anymore.

Then, they hear a voice. It is their teacher. She comes to see what is wrong.

"Why are you crying?" she asks. "What happened?"

They tell her their story. She listens and nods.

"I see," she says. "You both like to make castles, but you disagree on how to do it. That is okay. You can have different ideas. But you should not fight. You should share and respect each other. You can make a castle together, or you can make your own castles. But you should not break each other's blocks. That is not nice."

She helps them pick up the blocks. She gives them a hug.

"Do you want to be friends again?" she asks.

They look at each other. They nod.

"Yes," they say.

They smile. They say sorry. They hug.

They decide to make a castle together. They use yellow blocks and other colors. They make a wide and tall and pretty castle. They are happy. They are friends.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They wanted to make a cake for Mom. They had flour, eggs, milk and sugar. But they needed something else.

"Ben, we need salt for the cake. Mom always puts salt in the cake. It makes it yummy," Lily said.

"OK, Lily. I will supply the salt. You mix the flour and the eggs," Ben said.

Ben looked for the salt. He saw a big jar on the shelf. He climbed on a chair and reached for the jar. But the jar was too heavy for him. He dropped the jar and it broke on the floor. Salt spilled everywhere.

"Oh no, Ben! You made a big mess. Look at all the salt. It is fine and white. It looks like snow," Lily said.

"Sorry, Lily. I did not mean to drop the jar. I wanted to supply the salt for the cake. But now we have no salt. And Mom will be mad at us," Ben said.

Lily and Ben were sad. They did not know what to do. They heard Mom coming home. They hid behind the table.

"Hello, kids. I'm home. What are you doing in the kitchen?" Mom said.

She saw the broken jar and the salt on the floor. She was surprised.

"Wow, what happened here? Did you try to make a cake?" Mom said.

Lily and Ben came out from behind the table. They looked at Mom with big eyes.

"Mom, we are sorry. We wanted to make a cake for you. But we dropped the salt. We made a big mess. We are sorry," Lily and Ben said.

Mom smiled. She hugged Lily and Ben.

"It's OK, kids. I'm not mad at you. I'm happy that you wanted to make a cake for me. That's very sweet of you. But next time, please ask me for help. Salt is not good for cakes. It makes them salty. And you have to be careful with jars. They can break and hurt you," Mom said.

"OK, Mom. We will ask you for help next time. We love you, Mom," Lily and Ben said.

Mom cleaned up the mess. She found some chocolate and sprinkles. She helped Lily and Ben make a new cake. It was yummy and pretty. They ate the cake together. They were happy.

One day, Tommy had a plan. He decided to hide his oat under his napkin and pretend he ate it. He thought his mom would not notice and he would be free of oat forever. He smiled as he pushed his bowl away and asked for more juice.

But Tommy did not know that his mom was very smart. She saw the lump under his napkin and guessed what he did. She waited until he finished his juice and then said, "Tommy, I have a surprise for you. You can have anything you want for lunch today. Anything at all."

Tommy was very happy. He thought his plan worked and he could have his favorite food. He said, "I want pizza, mom. Pizza with cheese and pepperoni and olives. And ice cream for dessert. Can I have that, mom?"

His mom nodded and said, "Sure, Tommy. You can have that. But first, you have to finish your breakfast." She lifted his napkin and revealed his oat. Tommy's eyes widened and he gasped. He saw his mom's smile and knew he was in trouble. He realized he made a big mistake. He wished he ate his oat when he had the chance. He hated oat more than ever.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red car. They liked to drive the car around the room and make noises. Vroom, vroom, beep, beep!

One day, they found a strange bottle in the closet. It had a label that said "Shrink". They did not know what that word meant, but they were curious. They opened the bottle and sprayed some of the liquid on the car. The car became very small, like a bug. They were surprised and scared.

They tried to spray the car again, but the bottle was empty. They did not know how to make the car big again. They started to cry. They wanted their big red car back.

Their mom heard them crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw the tiny car and the bottle. She was angry and worried. She asked them what they did. They tried to tell her, but they could not. The liquid had also shrunk their language. They could only say simple words, like "car", "small", "sorry".

Their mom hugged them and said it was okay. She said she would find a way to fix the car and their language. She said they should never play with things they did not understand. She said they should always ask her first. She said she loved them.

She took them to the bathroom and washed their mouths with water and soap. The soap was smelly, but it helped. They started to say more words, like "mom", "love", "thank you".

She called a doctor and a mechanic. They came and helped. They gave them some medicine and some tools. They made the car big again and their language normal again. They were happy and relieved.

Ben and Lily learned a lesson. They said they would never spray anything again. They said they would always listen to their mom. They said they were sorry. They hugged their mom and their car. They played with their toys. They had fun. The end.

One day, the king had to go away for a long time. He said to Hairy, "I have to go to another place, but I will come back soon. You be a good dog and stay here with the queen. She will take care of you and play with you." Hairy wagged his tail and licked the king's face. He was sad, but he trusted the king.

The queen was nice, but she did not like Hairy very much. She thought he was too big and too dirty. She did not let him roll on the grass or sleep on the bed. She made him stay in a small room with no toys or bones. Hairy was bored and lonely. He missed the king and his fun.

One day, Hairy heard a loud noise outside. He looked out the window and saw a big truck with many men. They had guns and masks and they were trying to break into the house. Hairy barked and growled. He wanted to protect the queen and the house. He ran out of the room and down the stairs. He saw the men coming in and he jumped on them. He bit them and scratched them and made them run away. He was very brave and strong.

The queen heard the noise and came down. She saw Hairy and the men and she was very surprised and scared. She hugged Hairy and said, "Thank you, Hairy. You saved me and the house. You are a good dog and a hero. I am sorry I was mean to you. You can roll on the grass and sleep on the bed and have all the toys and bones you want." Hairy wagged his tail and licked the queen's face. He was happy and proud.

Soon, the king came back and heard what happened. He was very glad and proud of Hairy. He said to Hairy, "You are a good dog and a hero. You are my best friend and I love you." Hairy wagged his tail and licked the king's face. He was very happy and loved. He rolled on the grass with the king and the queen and lived happily ever after.

"Be careful with the thermometer, Sara. Don't bite it or drop it. It can break and hurt you," Mommy said.

Sara nodded and put the thermometer under her tongue. She waited for it to beep. She felt bored and tired. She wanted to play with her toys or watch TV. But Mommy said she had to stay in bed until she got better.

The thermometer beeped. Mommy took it out of Sara's mouth and looked at it. She frowned.

"Your fever is still high, Sara. You need to take some medicine and drink some water. Maybe you can read a book or listen to some music to pass the time," Mommy said.

She gave Sara a spoonful of medicine and a glass of water. Sara made a face. The medicine was bitter and the water was plain. She wished she had some juice or ice cream.

"Thank you, Mommy. I love you," Sara said.

"I love you too, Sara. I hope you feel better soon. I'll be back to check on you later," Mommy said.

She kissed Sara on the forehead and left the room. Sara put the book and the music player on her nightstand. She snuggled under the covers and closed her eyes. She hoped she would feel better soon. She missed playing and having fun.

One night, a little boy named Sam could not sleep. He heard a noise outside his window. He got up and looked out. He saw a big, brown owl sitting on a branch. The owl had yellow eyes and a sharp beak.

"Who are you?" Sam asked the owl.

"Who, who, who?" the owl said.

"I am Sam. I live in this house. Why are you here?" Sam said.

"I am Owl. I live in this tree. I am here to hunt for mice. Why are you awake?" Owl said.

"I can't sleep. I had a bad dream. Can you be my friend?" Sam said.

Owl was grumpy. He did not like to talk to humans. He liked to be alone and quiet. He wanted to turn away and fly to another tree. But he saw that Sam was sad and scared. He felt sorry for him.

"Okay, I can be your friend. For a little while. What was your bad dream about?" Owl said.

Sam told Owl about his dream. He dreamed that a big, black dog chased him and bit him. He was very afraid of dogs. Owl listened to Sam. He told him that dreams are not real. He said that he was brave and strong. He said that he would protect him from any dog.

Sam felt better. He thanked Owl for being his friend. He said that he liked owls. He asked Owl if he could see him again.

"Maybe. If you are quiet and respectful. And if you don't bother me when I am hunting. Owls are not pets. We are wild and free. But we can be friends. Sometimes." Owl said.

Sam nodded. He understood. He said good night to Owl. He went back to his bed. He closed his eyes. He felt safe and happy. He fell asleep.

Owl watched Sam for a while. He was not so grumpy anymore. He was glad that he helped Sam. He felt a little warm and fuzzy. He smiled. He turned his head and looked for a mouse. He flew away. He was still Owl. But he was also Sam's friend. Sometimes.

"Thank you, Ben!" Lily said. She hugged her snowman.

They played with their snowmen until they melted. They had a lot of fun. They learned that ice can grow and shrink with the sun. They also learned that bald snowmen need hats and scarves.
