The girl felt better after the doctor helped her. She learned not to spin too much and thanked the dog for rescuing her. From then on, she only spun a little bit at a time.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He lived in a house on a hill. Every morning, he would go for a walk in the fog. The fog was like a cloud on the ground. It was hard to see where he was going, but he liked it.

One day, the old man wanted to climb to the top of the hill. He tried and tried, but it was hard. He was tired and wanted to give up. But he didn't. He kept trying and trying until he succeeded! He was so happy that he could see the whole town from the top of the hill.

From then on, the old man knew that he could do anything if he just kept trying. And he still went for walks in the fog every morning, because he liked the way it made him feel.

Once upon a time, there was a big brown dog. He loved to play in the forest and chase after squirrels. One day, the dog saw an unusual log. It was very big and had lots of bumps on it. The dog sniffed the log and then tried to bite it. But the log was too hard and the dog hurt his teeth.

The dog went back to his house and told his owner about the unusual log. The owner went to see it and realized that it was not a log at all, but a big rock! The owner laughed and gave the dog a treat for being so curious. From then on, the dog knew to be careful when trying to bite things that looked unusual.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the garden with her toys. One day, she saw a long, scary dragon in the garden. She was very scared and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, she remembered what her mommy told her. She took a step back and started to think. She remembered that the dragon was scared of loud noises. She quickly grabbed her toy trumpet and blew it as loud as she could. The dragon got scared and ran away.

Lily learned that sometimes when we are scared, we just need to take a step back and think of a solution. She also learned that even though something looks scary, it might not be as bad as it seems. From that day on, she was never afraid of anything again.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play together. One day, Ben has a new toy. It is a car. The car is orange. It can make noises and move.

"Look, Mia, this is my car!" Ben says. He shows Mia his car. "It is orange. It is fast. Do you want to play with it?"

"Yes, please!" Mia says. She likes cars. She likes orange. She takes the car from Ben. She pushes the car on the floor. The car makes noises and moves. "Vroom, vroom!" Mia says. She smiles.

Ben smiles too. He is happy to share his car with Mia. He gets another toy. It is a truck. The truck is blue. It can carry things. "This is my truck!" Ben says. He shows Mia his truck. "It is blue. It is strong. Do you want to trade?"

"OK!" Mia says. She likes trucks. She likes blue. She gives the car to Ben. She takes the truck from him. She puts some blocks on the truck. The truck carries the blocks. "Beep, beep!" Mia says. She laughs.

Ben and Mia enjoy playing with the car and the truck. They trade them again and again. They make noises and stories. They have fun. They are good friends.

Lila and Max are friends. They like to play at the beach. They have a big towel to seat on. They also have a bucket and a shovel to make sand castles.

One day, a new girl comes to the beach. Her name is Mia. She has a pink towel and a pink bucket and a pink shovel. She seats next to Lila and Max. She says, "Hi, I'm Mia. Can I play with you?"

Lila and Max say, "Sure, you can play with us." They share their bucket and shovel with Mia. They make a big sand castle together. They have fun.

But then, Mia says, "Look at my towel. It's so pretty and soft. It's better than your towel. Your towel is old and rough. You should get a new towel like mine."

Lila and Max feel sad. They like their towel. It's big and cozy. It has many colors and shapes. They don't want a new towel. They think Mia is mean.

They say, "We don't like your towel. We like our towel. We don't want to play with you. You are jealous and rude. Go away."

Mia feels angry. She says, "Fine, I don't need you. I have my own towel and my own bucket and my own shovel. I can play by myself."

She takes her things and seats far away from Lila and Max. She tries to make a sand castle, but it falls down. She feels lonely and bored.

Lila and Max hug each other. They say, "We are happy. We have each other and we have our towel. We don't need anything else."

They smile and continue to play. They make a bigger and better sand castle. They have more fun.

Lily and Ben were going to visit their grandma. They had to pack their bags with clothes and toys. Lily packed her bag very fast. She put in her dress, her doll, her book and her hat. She did not leave any space for anything else.

Ben packed his bag very slow. He put in his shirt, his pants, his car and his pipe. His pipe was very light and made of wood. He liked to blow bubbles with it. He left some space for other things.

Lily saw Ben's pipe and wanted it. She said, "Give me your pipe. It is mine. I saw it first." Ben said, "No, it is mine. Grandma gave it to me. You have your doll." Lily got angry and tried to grab the pipe. Ben held it tight and said, "Stop it. You are being mean."

They started to fight over the pipe. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They did not hear their mom calling them. She came to their room and saw them fighting. She was very sad and said, "What are you doing? You are brother and sister. You should share and be kind. Fighting is not nice. How do you think grandma will feel if she sees you like this?"

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were selfish. We will not fight anymore." They hugged and said sorry to each other. Lily gave Ben his pipe and Ben gave Lily his car. They packed their bags again and made room for both. They smiled and said, "We are ready to go. We love you, mom. We love you, grandma." Mom smiled and said, "I love you, too. You are good children. Now let's go and have fun." They took their bags and went to the car. They were happy and excited to see their grandma.

Sam and Jen liked to go to the park with Mom. They liked to see the ducks and the geese that lived in the pond. Sometimes they gave them bread, but Mom said not too much.

One day, they saw a big white goose with a red beak. It looked very busy, swimming and honking and flapping its wings. Sam wanted to touch it. He asked Mom, "Can I touch the goose, please?"

Mom shook her head. "No, Sam, you can't touch the goose. It might bite you or chase you. It's not a pet, it's a wild animal. You have to be careful and respectful."

Sam was not happy. He wanted to touch the goose. He thought it was soft and fluffy. He waited until Mom was talking to Jen, and then he ran to the pond. He reached out his hand to the goose.

But the goose did not like that. It saw Sam and it got angry. It hissed and snapped at Sam's hand. Sam screamed and ran back to Mom. He had a red mark on his hand where the goose bit him.

Mom hugged Sam and put a band-aid on his hand. She said, "I told you not to touch the goose, Sam. You have to listen to me. The goose was busy and did not want to be bothered. You have to say sorry to the goose and leave it alone."

Sam looked at the goose. It was still busy, swimming and honking and flapping its wings. He felt sorry for the goose and for himself. He said, "Sorry, goose. I won't touch you again. You are very pretty, but not very friendly."

Lily was a small girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a doll, a ball, a car and a coat. She loved her coat. It was red and soft and warm. She wore it every day, even when it was not cold.

One night, Lily did not want to sleep. She wanted to play with her coat. She put it on and ran around her room. She pretended she was a superhero, a princess, a doctor and a teacher. She had fun, but she also made a lot of noise.

Her mom came to her room and said, "Lily, it is time to sleep. You have to take off your coat and put on your pajamas. You can play with your coat tomorrow."

Lily did not like that. She said, "No, mom, I want to keep my coat. It is my favorite. I need it to sleep."

Her mom said, "Lily, you cannot sleep with your coat. It is too hot and heavy. You will be sweaty and uncomfortable. Your coat needs to rest too. You can hang it on the hook and say good night to it."

Lily did not want to do that. She said, "No, mom, I want to hug my coat. It is my friend. It makes me happy and safe. Please, let me keep it."

Her mom was patient and kind. She said, "Lily, I understand that you love your coat, but you have to let it go. You have other friends to sleep with. You have your doll, your ball, your car and your teddy bear. They are all waiting for you in your bed. They will keep you company and protect you from bad dreams. You can give them a hug and a kiss and tell them a story. How about that?"

Lily thought about it. She looked at her toys and saw that they were lonely and sad. She felt sorry for them. She also felt a little hot and tired. She said, "Okay, mom, I will try. But can I say good night to my coat first?"

Her mom said, "Of course, you can. Go ahead and say good night to your coat. Tell it how much you love it and thank it for the fun you had today. Then, hang it on the hook and come to bed."

Lily did as her mom said. She hugged her coat and said, "Good night, coat. I love you very much. You are the best coat in the world. Thank you for playing with me today. You are a great superhero, a princess, a doctor and a teacher. I will see you tomorrow. Sleep well, coat."

She hung her coat on the hook and went to bed. She put on her pajamas and crawled under the covers. She hugged her doll, her ball, her car and her teddy bear. She said, "Good night, friends. I love you too. You are also the best in the world. Thank you for being with me tonight. You are a great team. Let's have a good sleep and dream of nice things."

She closed her eyes and fell asleep. Her mom smiled and kissed her forehead. She said, "Good night, Lily. I love you more than anything. You are my sweet and brave girl. Sleep tight and sweet dreams."

She turned off the light and left the room. She was proud of Lily for letting go of her coat and sleeping with her toys. She hoped that Lily would have a peaceful and happy night. She also hoped that Lily would not miss her coat too much in the morning.

Anna hears a loud sound. She looks at the dress and sees a big hole in it. She looks at Lily and sees her arm is broken. Anna starts to cry. She has ruined the dress and hurt Lily. She wishes she had not tried to stretch the dress. She wishes she had been more careful and useful. She thinks maybe her mom can fix the dress and Lily, but she is afraid her mom will be mad at her. She does not know what to do. She feels very bad.

Tommy was a little boy who liked to drink milk every morning. He had a blue cup with a picture of a cow on it. He always asked his mom for milk when he woke up.

One day, Tommy woke up and saw that his mom was not in the kitchen. He went to look for her and found her in the bathroom. She was brushing her teeth and putting on her coat. She looked busy and tired.

"Mom, I want milk!" Tommy said.

"Sorry, honey, we don't have any milk today. The store was closed yesterday and we ran out. You can have some juice or water instead." Mom said.

Tommy did not like juice or water. He only liked milk. He felt angry and sad. He started to complain.

"No, no, no! I want milk! Milk, milk, milk!" He shouted. He stomped his feet and threw his blue cup on the floor. It made a loud noise and broke into pieces.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the broken cup and the mess on the floor. She saw Tommy crying and screaming. She felt unhappy and frustrated. She tried to calm him down.

"Tommy, stop it! You can't have milk today. It's not here. You have to drink something else. And you can't break your cup. That's not nice. You have to be careful with your things." She said.

Tommy did not listen. He kept complaining. He did not want something else. He did not care about his cup. He only wanted milk.

Mom did not know what to do. She had to go to work soon. She had no time to clean up or to buy milk. She felt uncomfortable and stressed. She wished Tommy would stop complaining and be a good boy. She wished she had some milk.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play at the beach. They liked to build sand castles, find shells, and splash in the water. One day, they saw a big boat on the ocean. It was white and shiny, and it made a loud noise.

"Let's go see the boat!" Ben said. He ran to the water and tried to swim to the boat. Lily followed him, but she was scared. The water was deep and cold, and the boat was far away.

"Ben, come back!" Lily shouted. "The boat is too big and too fast. We can't catch it. We can get hurt."

But Ben did not listen. He wanted to see the boat up close. He swam and swam, but the boat did not get closer. It got smaller and smaller, until it was gone. Ben was confused. Where did the boat go? He looked around and saw that he was alone. He could not see Lily or the beach. He was lost.

He started to cry. He was cold and tired and scared. He wished he had listened to Lily. He wished he had stayed on the sand. He did not know what to do.

Lily was worried. She could not see Ben. She did not know where he went. She hoped he was okay. She stood on the shore and waved her arms. She hoped someone would see her and help her. She hoped someone would find Ben and bring him back.

She saw a man on a jet ski. He was wearing a red jacket and a helmet. He saw Lily and came to her. He asked her what was wrong. She told him about Ben and the boat. He nodded and said he would look for Ben. He told Lily to stay on the beach and wait for him. He gave her a blanket and a bottle of water. He zoomed away on the jet ski.

Lily waited and prayed. She hoped the man would find Ben. She hoped Ben was okay. She felt sorry for being angry at Ben. She loved her brother. She wanted him to be safe.

After a long time, she saw the man come back. He had Ben with him. Ben was wet and shivering, but he was alive. He hugged Lily and said he was sorry. He said he was stupid and foolish. He said he learned his lesson. He said he would never swim away from Lily again.

Lily hugged him back and said she was sorry too. She said she was glad he was okay. She said she learned her lesson too. She said she would never follow Ben into danger again.

The man smiled and said they were brave and smart kids. He said they should always listen to each other and stay close to each other. He said they should always respect the ocean and its power. He said they should always be careful and have fun. He took them back to their parents, who were very happy and relieved to see them. They thanked the man and hugged their kids. They said they were proud of them and loved them.

Ben and Lily learned a lot that day. They learned to be more careful, more respectful, and more loving. They learned to enjoy the ocean, but not to chase the boats. They learned to stand by each other, but not to follow each other blindly. They learned to be happy and grateful for what they had. They learned a valuable lesson.

She put the ring on her finger and felt like a princess. She wondered who put the ring in the ice cell. She wondered if there were more ice cells in the freezer. She ran to look.

The little boy asked his mum what was wrong. She said it was too old. The little boy had forgotten to check the date before he ate it. He was very sad that he had made a mistake and wasted his cereal.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old.

One day, Lucy went for a walk in the park. As she wandered, the grass tickled her toes. She smiled and kept walking.

Suddenly, she heard a funny sound. She looked around and saw that the grass was trembling. Lucy was scared and started to tremble too!

The trembling seemed to be coming from the big, wet lawn. She had to go and take a closer look. Cautiously, she stepped closer.

The lawn started to tremble even more! What could it be? Suddenly, she heard a loud quack! Lucy peered closer and saw two ducks swimming on the wet lawn.
      
The ducks were quaking, and they looked scared! Lucy realized they were just scared of her. She smiled, and the ducks stopped trembling.

Lucy waved goodbye to the ducks and they swam away. She laughed, happy that she could help the ducks. Lucy left the wet lawn, feeling proud of herself.

Once upon a time there was a bald daddy who had a wallet. His little daughter was very curious and she wanted to see inside the wallet. Surprisingly, the daddy said no. The little girl was very disappointed and started to cry.

But then, a big boy comes and snatches her notebook. He says it is his and he runs away. Lily is very sad and angry. She cries and shouts. She wants her notebook back. She tries to chase the big boy, but he is too fast. She falls down and scrapes her knee. It hurts a lot.

Lily's mom hears her cry and runs to her. She hugs her and asks what happened. Lily tells her about the big boy and her notebook. She shows her mom her hurt knee. Her mom says she is sorry and kisses her knee. She says they will find the big boy and get her notebook back.

Lily and her mom look around the park. They see the big boy sitting on a bench. He is looking at Lily's notebook. He does not see them. Lily's mom walks up to him and says, "Excuse me, that is not your notebook. That is Lily's notebook. She wrote and drew in it. Please give it back to her."

The big boy looks up and sees Lily and her mom. He feels scared and ashamed. He says he is sorry and hands the notebook to Lily. He says he liked her pictures and wanted to see them. He says he did not mean to hurt her. Lily takes her notebook and says thank you. She says she is glad he likes her pictures, but he should not take things that are not his. She says he can write and draw in his own notebook.

Lily and her mom smile and walk away. Lily is happy to have her notebook back. She says she forgives the big boy, but he should be nicer. She says she wants to write and draw some more. Her mom says she is proud of her. They sit under the big tree and write and draw together. They have fun.

Tom is a fisherman. He likes to catch fish in the sea. He has a big boat and a big net. He goes to the sea every day.

One day, Tom sees a big fish in the water. He wants to catch it. He throws his net into the water. But the fish is too strong. It pulls the net and the boat. Tom is scared.

Tom tries to call for help. But he is deaf. He cannot hear. He cannot talk. He does not have a phone. He does not know what to do.

Then he sees a plane in the sky. The plane is flying low. It is looking for something. Tom has an idea. He takes his red shirt and waves it in the air. He hopes the plane will see him.

The plane sees Tom and his red shirt. It flies closer. It sees the fish and the net and the boat. It understands. It sends a radio message to another boat. The other boat comes to help Tom.

Tom is happy. He raises his hand and smiles. He thanks the plane and the other boat. He lets the fish go. He does not want to catch it anymore. He goes back to the shore. He is safe.

They looked at each other and felt sad. They wanted to read the book, but they could not. They decided to close the book and return it to the shelf. They said sorry to the book for not reading it.

They went to another shelf and found a book that was not too old and not too hard. It had a picture of a dog and a cat on the cover. They opened the book and read the words. They understood them. They smiled and laughed. They enjoyed the book.

Sam was sad. He wanted to ride the mule too. He said to Tom, "That is not fair. You always get what you want. Let me ride the mule too."

Tom said, "No, you are too small. You will fall off the mule. Go away and leave me alone."

Sam was angry. He picked up a rock and threw it at Tom. The rock hit Tom on the head. Tom cried out and fell off the mule.

A big truck was coming on the road. The truck driver did not see the mule. He hit the mule with the truck. The mule was hurt. It made a loud noise and lay on the ground.

Tom and Sam heard the noise. They ran to the road. They saw the mule and the truck. They were sorry. They wished they had not fought. They wished they had been nice to the mule.

But it was too late. The mule was gone. Tom and Sam were sad. They learned a hard lesson. They said to each other, "We are sorry. We will not be bossy or throw rocks again. We will share and be kind."

Mom hears Anna and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the card and the poppy. She hugs Anna and says, "I'm sorry, sweetie. Poppies are very delicate. They need water and sun to stay alive. When you pick them, they die quickly. You can't design with them."

Anna feels sad. She says, "But I wanted to make something pretty for you."

Mom smiles and says, "You did, honey. You made something very pretty. And you made something very kind. You wanted to share the poppy with me. That is very sweet of you. I love you very much."

Anna feels a little better. She says, "I love you too, Mom."

Mom says, "Why don't we go back to the garden and see if we can find some other flowers that we can design with? Maybe some daisies or roses or sunflowers. They are stronger and last longer. And they are very pretty too."

Anna nods and says, "OK, Mom. Let's go."

They hold hands and walk to the garden. They look for flowers that they can design with. They have fun and make beautiful things. Anna is happy again.

"Can we have some apples?" Lily asked Tom.

One day, Tom saw a little dog on the road. The dog was lost and scared. Tom did not stop to help the dog. He wanted to speed and have fun. He laughed and drove faster. He did not see the big truck coming from the other side.

The truck driver saw Tom and the dog. He was a good man. He loved animals. He tried to slow down and honk his horn. He wanted to warn Tom and save the dog. But it was too late. Tom was going too fast. He could not stop or turn. He crashed into the truck with a big bang.

The truck driver and the dog were okay. They had some bumps and bruises, but they were alive. The truck driver got out of his truck and ran to the dog. He hugged the dog and said, "Don't worry, little one. You are safe now. I will take you home and be your friend."

Lily and Ben are sad. They cry. They wish they had listened to Mom. They wish they had shared. They wish they had given each other space. They hug and say sorry. They decide to play something else. They are not competitive anymore.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big brown pie on a table. It smells good. They want to eat it.

"Let's have some pie," Anna says.

"No, we can't," Ben says. "It is not ours. It is for someone else."

"But I am hungry," Anna says. "And it looks yummy."

She runs to the table and takes a big bite of the pie. Ben follows her and tries to stop her.

"Stop, Anna, stop!" he says. "You are being bad. You are taking what is not yours."

But Anna does not listen. She eats more and more of the pie. She makes a mess. She gets pie on her face and her clothes.

Then, they hear a voice.

"Hey, what are you doing?" the voice says. "That is my pie. I made it for my grandma. She is sick and I wanted to make her happy."

Anna and Ben look up. They see a boy standing by the table. He looks angry and sad. He is holding a basket and a card.

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They know they did something wrong. They say sorry to the boy.

"We are sorry," they say. "We did not know. We were hungry and the pie looked good. We are very sorry."

The boy looks at them. He sees the pie on their faces and clothes. He sees the hole in his pie. He feels bad for his grandma. But he also feels sorry for Anna and Ben. He knows they are just kids.

He says, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you should not take things that are not yours. It is not nice. And you should not waste food. It is not good."

He gives them a napkin and helps them clean up. He says, "Do you want to help me make another pie for my grandma? I have some more ingredients in my basket. We can share it with her. Maybe she will feel better."

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, please. We want to help. We want to make your grandma happy."

They follow the boy to his house. They help him make another pie. They make it big and brown and yummy. They write a card for his grandma. They say, "We are sorry for eating your pie. We hope you like this one. We hope you get well soon. We are your new friends, Anna and Ben."

They take the pie and the card to his grandma. She is lying in bed. She looks tired and pale. But when she sees the pie and the card, she smiles. She says, "Thank you, thank you. You are very kind. You made my day. Come, sit with me. Let's have some pie together."

They sit with her and have some pie. They talk and laugh. They become friends. They learn a lesson. They are happy.

After a long time, someone finally noticed that they were missing. They found them in the toilet, but it was too late. Lily and her mommy were very cold and sick. From that day on, they always made sure to check the toilet before they went inside.

Lila and Tom were scared. They tried to run, but they were too weak. They fell to the floor. They cried and screamed. But no one heard them. No one helped them. The old woman grabbed them and dragged them to the pot. She threw them in and stirred them with a big spoon. She said, "Goodbye, little ones. Thank you for your flesh and bones. Thank you for your souls and dreams. You are the best dinner I ever had."

"I'm Max and this is Spot," the boy says. "Your parrot is very pretty. Can he do tricks?"

"Yes, he can," Sara says proudly. "Coco, can you say hello to Max and Spot?"

"Hello, hello, hello!" Coco says in a loud voice. He flaps his wings and bobs his head.

"Wow, that's amazing!" Max says. "Can I pet him?"

"Sure, but be gentle," Sara says. "He likes to be scratched on his head."

Max reaches out his hand and gently strokes Coco's feathers. Coco makes a happy sound and nibbles on Max's finger.

"Ouch, that tickles!" Max says, laughing.

"He likes you," Sara says, smiling. "Do you want to play with us?"

"Yes, please," Max says. "Can I wear your hat?"

"Okay, but only if I can wear yours," Sara says.

They swap their hats and run around the park, pretending to be pirates. Coco flies after them, joining in their fun. They have a great time together. Sara and Max become new friends, and so do Coco and Spot.

Lily liked to draw with her pen. She drew flowers and trees and birds on her paper. She was very proud of her drawings. She wanted to show them to her mom and dad.

She ran to the living room, where her mom and dad were watching TV. She said, "Look, look, what I drew! Can I display them on the wall?"

Her mom and dad smiled and said, "Sure, Lily, you can display them on the wall. But be careful, don't make a mess."

Lily was very happy. She took some tape and stuck her drawings on the wall. She made a big display of her art. She said, "See, see, how pretty they are!"

But then, something bad happened. The tape was not strong enough. The drawings fell off the wall. They landed on the floor. And then, the dog came. The dog was wild. He liked to chew on things. He saw the drawings and thought they were toys. He ran to the floor and grabbed the drawings with his teeth. He tore them and bit them and made them into pieces.

Lily saw what the dog did. She was very sad. She cried and cried. She said, "No, no, stop it! You ruined my drawings! They were mine!"

Her mom and dad heard her cry. They came to the living room and saw the mess. They were very angry. They said, "Lily, what did you do? You made a big mess! And you upset the dog! You should not display your drawings on the wall. You should keep them in your folder. Now, go to your room and think about what you did."

Lily had to go to her room. She had no drawings left. She had no pen left. The dog had eaten it too. She had nothing to draw with. She felt very sorry. She wished she had listened to her mom and dad. She wished she had not displayed her drawings on the wall. She wished the dog had not been wild. She wished she had a happy ending. But she did not. She had a bad ending.

Lily and Ben were playing with a big ball in the living room. They liked to throw the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they threw the ball very high and it hit the ceiling. The ceiling was white and smooth and made a loud noise when the ball hit it.

"Pass me the ball, Lily!" Ben shouted. He was ready to catch it with his hands.

"OK, Ben!" Lily said. She threw the ball as hard as she could. But she threw it too high and too far. The ball flew over Ben's head and hit the window. The window broke and the ball fell outside.

"Oh no!" Lily and Ben said together. They were scared and sad. They liked the ball and they did not want to break the window.

They heard a grumpy voice from the kitchen. It was their mom. She was making lunch and she heard the noise.

"What was that?" Mom asked. She came to the living room and saw the broken window and the ball outside. She was angry and worried.

"Lily and Ben, what did you do?" Mom asked. She looked at them with a stern face.

"We were playing with the ball, Mom," Lily said. She felt sorry and guilty.

"We threw the ball too high, Mom," Ben said. He felt sorry and guilty too.

"You know you are not supposed to play with the ball inside the house," Mom said. "You could hurt yourselves or damage something. Now the window is broken and we have to fix it. And the ball is gone. How do you feel about that?"

Lily and Ben felt very bad. They knew they made a mistake and they upset their mom.

"We feel very bad, Mom," Lily said. "We are sorry we broke the window and lost the ball."

"We are sorry we made you angry and worried, Mom," Ben said. "We will not play with the ball inside the house again."

Mom sighed. She was still angry and worried, but she also loved her children. She knew they were young and they did not mean to cause trouble.

"I love you, Lily and Ben," Mom said. "But you have to be more careful and follow the rules. Playing with the ball is fun, but you have to play with it outside or in a safe place. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom," Lily and Ben said. They hugged their mom and said they loved her too.

Mom smiled. She was still grumpy, but she also felt a little better. She decided to make some cookies for dessert and to call Dad to help with the window. She hoped they could find the ball later and play with it again. But only outside.

Tom did not like Lily's demand. He said, "No, this is my car. You have your doll. Go play with your doll."

Lily was angry. She said, "No, I want your car. It is more fun than my doll. Give it to me now!"

Tom was angry too. He said, "No, you can't have my car. It is mine. Go away!"

Lily did not go away. She tried to grab Tom's car from his hands. Tom tried to hold on to his car. They both pulled and tugged at the car. They did not see that they were near the stairs.

The car slipped from their hands and rolled down the stairs. It crashed into the wall and broke into pieces. Lily and Tom were shocked. They ran down the stairs to see their car. They felt very sad and sorry.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the broken car and the sad twins. She said, "What did you do? Why did you break your car?"

Lily and Tom told their mom what happened. They said they were sorry and that they did not mean to break the car. They said they were clumsy and foolish.

Their mom was not happy. She said, "You should not fight over your toys. You should share and take turns. You should be kind and gentle. You should say please and thank you. You should be a good sister and a good brother."

Lily and Tom nodded. They said they were sorry and that they would be better. They hugged their mom and said they loved her.

Their mom hugged them back and said she loved them too. She said, "I have a surprise for you. Come with me."

She took them to the living room. There was a big box with a bow on it. She said, "This is a welcome gift for you. I got it for you because you are going to have a new baby brother or sister soon. Do you want to see what is inside?"

Lily and Tom were curious and excited. They said, "Yes, please. Can we open it?"

Their mom said, "Yes, you can. But be careful. It is fragile."

Lily and Tom opened the box. Inside was a big teddy bear. It was soft and fluffy and had a cute smile. Lily and Tom smiled too. They liked the teddy bear. They said, "Thank you, mom. This is a nice gift. We love it."

Their mom said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you like it. This is your new friend. You can play with it together. But remember, you have to share and take turns. You have to be kind and gentle. You have to say please and thank you. You have to be a good sister and a good brother. Can you do that?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They said, "Yes, we can. We will do that. We will be good."

Their mom smiled. She said, "That's good. I'm proud of you. Now, why don't you give your new friend a name?"

Lily and Tom thought for a moment. Then they said, "We will name it Car-Doll. Because it is a mix of our toys. And because we learned our lesson."

Their mom laughed. She said, "That's a funny and clever name. I like it. Car-Doll it is. Now, why don't you give Car-Doll a hug and say hello?"

Lily and Tom hugged Car-Doll and said hello. They felt happy and warm. They looked at their mom and said, "We love you, mom. And we love Car-Doll. And we love our new baby brother or sister. We are a happy family."

Their mom said, "I love you too, Lily and Tom. And I love Car-Doll. And I love our new baby too. We are a happy family indeed."

Anna frowned and said, "No, it's not. It's fun and cool. Watch, I'll show you." She plugged the iron into the wall and turned it on. She waited for a few seconds, and then she pressed the iron on a shirt. The iron made a loud hissing sound and steam came out.

One night, Lily had an idea. She whispered to Max, "Let's sneak out of our room and get some chocolate from the kitchen. Mom won't know. We can eat it under the table and then go back to sleep."

Max nodded. He was impatient to taste the sweet chocolate. They waited until their mom turned off the light and went to her room. Then they tiptoed out of their room and down the stairs. They found the chocolate in the cupboard and took two pieces each. They crawled under the table and unwrapped the chocolate.

"Mmm, this is so good," Lily said, biting into her chocolate.

"Shh, be quiet," Max said, "or mom will hear us."

They ate their chocolate quickly and licked their fingers. They felt happy and full. They decided to go back to their room and sleep. But as they got up from under the table, they heard a voice.

"What are you two doing here?" It was their mom. She had heard them and came to check on them. She saw the chocolate wrappers on the floor and the chocolate on their faces.

Lily and Max felt scared and guilty. They knew they had done something wrong. They hung their heads and said, "Sorry, mom. We wanted to eat chocolate and we didn't want to sleep."

Their mom sighed. She was not happy, but she was not angry either. She loved her twins, even when they were naughty. She said, "You know you have to sleep at night, right? Chocolate is not good for you before bed. It can give you bad dreams and tummy aches. And you have to brush your teeth after eating chocolate, or you will get cavities."

Lily and Max nodded. They understood. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We won't do it again. Can we have a hug?"

Their mom hugged them and kissed them. She said, "I forgive you. But you have to promise me to sleep well tonight and to eat chocolate only as a treat sometimes, not every night. OK?"

Lily and Max promised. They said, "OK, mom. We love you."

Their mom said, "I love you too. Now let's go to your room and brush your teeth and tuck you in."

Lily and Max followed their mom to their room. They brushed their teeth and put on their pajamas. Their mom tucked them in and read them a story. They felt cozy and sleepy. They closed their eyes and dreamed of chocolate.

He had found a treasure map and wanted to bury it with her in the backyard. Together, they dug another hole and buried the treasure map.

From that day on, Lily and Mr. Brown had a lot of fun digging and burying treasures in the backyard. They became good friends and always looked out for each other.

And ever since that day, the wise little bird has never quit the big twig. It sits there every day singing its songs, enjoying the peace and quiet of the forest.

The lonely pony was never lonely again.

But then he peeked over and saw it was just a pretty firefly. The firefly was sending out light in the dark night and it was so pretty. The giraffe was so happy he didn't let the noise scare him. He just laughed, hopped back up and kept walking.

Once upon a time, there was a pink potato. It wanted to march forward, but it was stuck in one spot. It saw a big, black bird fly above its head and thought to itself, "If only I could fly like that bird, I could march anywhere I wanted."

The pink potato was so determined to march that it thought hard and long about how to fly. Finally, it figured out a way. It lifted up its stem and began to flap it back and forth. It was working! 

The pink potato kept on flapping until the stem became too heavy and it fell back to the ground. It didn't give up though. It had a plan. It rolled down a hill, and as it did, it kept on flapping its stem. The wind caught it and lifted it up and carried it farther and farther away.

Now, the pink potato is free to march all around. It floats in the sky and marches from flower to flower, all the while waving goodbye with its stem.

The End.

"Yes, please!" Floppy hopped excitedly. "What do you want to play?"

"I know a fun game!" Tweetie said. "Let's see who can count to zero the fastest."

"Okay!" Floppy agreed. "But how do we count to zero?"

"It's easy," Tweetie explained. "We start at one and keep saying the next number until we get to zero. Ready, set, go!"

Floppy and Tweetie began counting. They went, "One, two, three, four, five..." But then Floppy got confused and said, "Six, seven, eight, nine, ten!"

"Oh no!" Tweetie said. "You skipped zero! That means you lose."

Ben and Lily were confused. They did not know what harvest meant. They did not want to eat their plants. They wanted to keep them as flowers. They looked at each other and shook their heads.

Mom looked at their plants and shook her head. "That's what happens when you don't harvest your cauliflowers, my dears. They spoil and rot. They are not flowers. They are food. You have to pick them when they are ripe, or they go to waste."

Ben and Lily felt sorry. They realized that they made a mistake. They wasted their plants and their food. They wished they had listened to mom. They learned a lesson.

"Mom, we are sorry. We were wrong. We should have harvested our cauliflowers. Can we try again?" they asked.

"Yes, really. And you know what? Sometimes, after thunder, there is a rainbow. A rainbow is very pretty. It has many colors. Do you like rainbows?" Anna asked.

Lily nodded. She liked rainbows. They were pretty and happy.

"Maybe we can see a rainbow if we wait a little. Do you want to wait with me?" Anna asked.

Lily thought for a moment. She was still a little worried. But she was also curious. And she liked Anna. She was a good friend.

"OK. I will wait with you. But can we hold hands?" Lily asked.

"Of course. We can hold hands. And we can finish our tea. And we can sing a song. Do you know a song?" Anna asked.

Lily smiled. She knew a song. She liked to sing.

"Yes, I know a song. It is about a star. Do you want to sing with me?" Lily asked.

"Yes, I want to sing with you. Let's sing together," Anna said.

They held hands. They finished their tea. They sang a song. They waited for the thunder to stop. And they saw a rainbow.

They enjoyed their tea party very much.

The moral value of the story is: friendship can help us overcome our fears.

Lily and Ben were playing on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shells and stones. Sometimes they found oysters, which had shiny pearls inside. Lily and Ben loved pearls. They wanted to make necklaces and bracelets with them.

One day, they found a big oyster. It was the biggest oyster they had ever seen. They opened it carefully and saw a beautiful pearl. It was white and round and shiny. Lily and Ben gasped.

"Wow, look at this pearl!" Lily said. "It is so pretty!"

"I want it!" Ben said. "I want to make a ring with it!"

"No, I want it!" Lily said. "I want to make a pendant with it!"

They both reached for the pearl, but they pulled too hard. The pearl flew out of their hands and rolled into the water.

"Oh no!" Lily and Ben cried. "We lost the pearl!"

They ran to the water and tried to find it, but it was too deep and too dark. They could not see the pearl. They felt sad and angry.

They started to blame each other.

"It is your fault!" Lily said. "You pulled too hard!"

"No, it is your fault!" Ben said. "You pulled too hard!"

They stopped being friends and turned away from each other.

A fish was swimming nearby. He saw the pearl and picked it up with his mouth. He saw Lily and Ben and felt sorry for them. He decided to be generous and help them.

He swam to the shore and spit out the pearl. He made a loud ring with his mouth to get their attention.

Lily and Ben heard the ring and looked at the water. They saw the fish and the pearl. They could not believe their eyes.

"Look, the fish has the pearl!" Lily said.

"He is giving it back to us!" Ben said.

They ran to the fish and thanked him.

"Thank you, fish!" Lily said. "You are very kind and generous!"

"Thank you, fish!" Ben said. "You are very smart and friendly!"

The fish smiled and swam away.

Lily and Ben looked at the pearl. They felt sorry for fighting.

"I am sorry, Lily," Ben said. "You can have the pearl. You can make a pendant with it."

"I am sorry, Ben," Lily said. "You can have the pearl. You can make a ring with it."

They hugged and smiled.

They decided to share the pearl. They made a necklace with it and took turns wearing it. They were happy and friends again.

When they landed, Lily felt very cold because of the icy weather. "Brrr, it's so cold!" she said. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we'll keep you warm." They all put on their warm jackets and went to explore the beautiful mountains. Lily had so much fun playing in the snow!

But Bear was selfish. He wanted all the honey for himself. He said, "No, Bee, this is my honey. You go away. I am bigger and stronger than you. You cannot have any."

Bee was sad and angry. He said, "That is not fair, Bear. You are being selfish. We are friends. We should share the honey. If you do not share, I will sting you."

Bear laughed. He said, "You cannot sting me, Bee. You are too small and weak. I have thick fur and sharp claws. You cannot hurt me. Go away or I will eat you."

Bee did not go away. He called his friends, the other bees. They came and saw the jar of honey and the selfish bear. They said, "We will help you, Bee. We will sting the bear until he gives up the honey. He cannot eat us all."

The bees flew around the bear and stung him on his nose, his ears, his paws, and his tail. The bear howled and cried. He said, "Stop, stop, bees. You are hurting me. I am sorry. I will share the honey. Please, do not sting me anymore."

The bees stopped. They said, "You are very selfish, bear. You should not take all the honey. You should be kind and share with your friends. If you are not, we will sting you again. Do you understand?"

The bear nodded. He said, "I understand, bees. I am sorry, Bee. You are my friend. I will share the honey with you. Please, forgive me."

Bee smiled. He said, "I forgive you, Bear. You are my friend, too. Let's eat the honey together. But we should also leave some for the other animals. They might like some, too."

The bear agreed. He said, "You are right, Bee. We should not be selfish. We should be generous. Let's leave some honey for the other animals. They will be happy."

The bee and the bear ate some honey and left some for the other animals. They were happy and full. They thanked each other and hugged. They learned to share and not to be selfish. They remained friends. The end.

"No, Tom, it is too dark and dirty. And what if there is a snake or a spider or a monster?" Lily said. "Let's go back to Spot. He is waiting for us."

Tom ignored Lily and went closer to the hole. He leaned over and tried to see what was inside. But he slipped and fell into the hole. He screamed and cried. He hurt his knee and his elbow.

Lily heard Tom and ran to the hole. She was very worried. She called for Spot, who came running. She saw Tom at the bottom of the hole. He looked very sad and scared.

"Tom, are you okay?" Lily shouted. "I'm sorry I ignored you. I was afraid of the hole. But I'm here now. And Spot is here too. We will help you get out."

Tom looked up and saw Lily and Spot. He felt a little better. He said, "I'm sorry too, Lily. I was silly and curious. I should have listened to you. The hole is not fun. It is scary and hurtful. Can you please help me get out?"

Lily nodded and said, "Of course, Tom. We are twins. We stick together. Spot, can you find a rope or a branch or something to pull Tom out?"

Spot barked and ran to look for something. He soon came back with a long rope that he found near a tent. He dropped it into the hole. Lily and Spot pulled the rope and Tom grabbed it. They pulled and pulled until Tom was out of the hole. He hugged Lily and Spot and thanked them.

They all went back to their home. They told their mom what happened. She was glad they were safe. She cleaned Tom's wounds and gave him a band-aid and a kiss. She also gave Lily and Spot a hug and a treat. She said, "You are very brave and kind, Lily and Spot. You helped Tom when he was in trouble. And you are very lucky, Tom, to have such a good sister and a good dog. Next time, be more careful and don't ignore your sister. She loves you and knows what is best for you."

Tom, Lily and Spot nodded and smiled. They learned their lesson. They never went near the hole again. They played in the forest, but they always stayed together and listened to each other. They were happy and safe.

But then, he saw the little girl's mommy coming towards him. He got scared and ran away, leaving the apple behind. From that day on, the wolf learned that stealing was not nice and it made others sad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her yard. One day, she saw her neighbor's swing and asked her mom if she could have one too. Her mom said they couldn't afford it because they weren't rich.

Lily was sad, but she didn't give up. She asked her grandpa if he could make her a swing. He said he could, but it would take some time. Lily was patient and waited.

Finally, one day, her grandpa surprised her with a swing he had made just for her. Lily was so happy and thanked her grandpa. She played on the swing every day and even invited her friends over to play too.

One day, while Lily was swinging, her neighbor came over and asked if she could play too. Lily said, "Of course! Let's swing together!" From that day on, Lily and her neighbor became good friends and played on the swing together all the time.

Suddenly, Lily saw smoke coming from the park's playground. Everyone started to panic and run away. Lily remembered her toy matches and realized she left them in her pocket. She quickly threw them away and ran to help her mom and the other people. Thanks to Lily's obedience, she saved the day and everyone admired her bravery.

Mickey saw the hard carrot and didn't know what to do either. He shrugged his shoulders and said, "I don't know how to help you." Benny was sad, but then he had an idea. He remembered that his mom used to cook carrots to make them soft.

So, Benny and Mickey went to Benny's mom and asked her to cook the hard carrot. Benny's mom boiled the carrot until it was soft and yummy. Benny was happy and thanked his mom and Mickey for their help. From that day on, Benny knew that if he found a hard carrot, he just needed to cook it to make it soft.

But then the sun goes down and it gets dark. They can't see the ball well. They don't want to stop playing. They want to record more.

"Let's do one more hit," Sam says. He holds the bat and waits for Tom to throw the ball.

"OK, but be careful," Tom says. He picks up the ball and throws it fast.

Sam swings the bat and hits the ball. But he does not see where it goes. He hears a loud crash. He drops the bat and runs to the camera.

"Oh no!" he cries. "The ball hit the camera and broke it!"

Tom runs to him and sees the broken camera. He is sad and angry.

"You broke the camera!" he yells. "Now we can't show our game to anyone!"

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" Sam says. "I didn't mean to!"

But Tom does not listen. He pushes Sam and they start to fight. They forget about the baseball and the fun. They only hurt each other.

Anna liked to visit her uncle Tom. He was very popular in his town. He had a big shop with many things. He sold fruits, vegetables, bread, cheese, and more. He was always nice to Anna and gave her a treat when she came.

One day, Anna went to the shop with her mom. She saw uncle Tom weigh some apples for a lady. He put the apples on a scale and looked at the numbers. Then he told the lady how much money she had to pay.

"Can I try?" Anna asked uncle Tom.

"Sure, sweetie. Here, take this basket of oranges and put them on the scale," uncle Tom said.

Anna lifted the basket with both hands. It was heavy. She walked slowly to the scale and put the basket on it. She looked at the numbers. They were bigger than the ones for the apples.

"Wow, you are strong, Anna. The oranges weigh more than the apples. Do you know how much they weigh?" uncle Tom asked.

Anna shook her head. She did not know.

"They weigh five kilos. That means five bags of sugar. Can you say five kilos?" uncle Tom said.

"Five kilos," Anna repeated.

"Very good. You are smart, Anna. Do you want an orange as a treat?" uncle Tom said.

"Yes, please. Thank you, uncle Tom. I love you," Anna said.

"I love you too, Anna. You are my favorite niece," uncle Tom said.

He gave her a big hug and an orange. Anna smiled and ate the orange. It was juicy and sweet. She was happy. She liked to visit her uncle Tom.

Ben says, "You can use my bat. We can share. We are friends."

Tim and Ben hug. They pick up their bats. They go back to play baseball. They are happy.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big boot on a bench. It was brown and shiny. Lily wanted to try it on. She said to Tom, "Look, a boot! Can I wear it?"

Tom said, "No, Lily. That is not your boot. That is someone else's boot. You cannot take it. That is stealing. Stealing is bad."

Lily did not listen. She said, "But I like it. It is pretty. I want it." She ran to the bench and grabbed the boot. She put it on her foot. It was too big for her. She fell down and hurt her knee.

Tom ran to help her. He said, "Lily, are you okay? You should not have taken the boot. That was wrong. You should say sorry."

Lily was sad. She said, "I am sorry, Tom. You are right. I should not have taken the boot. That was rude. I will give it back."

They saw a man coming to the bench. He was looking for his boot. He said, "Hey, where is my boot? Who took my boot?"

Lily and Tom were scared. They said, "We are sorry, sir. We took your boot. We did not mean to. We will give it back to you."

The man was angry. He said, "You took my boot? Why did you do that? That is stealing. You should not steal. That is not polite."

Lily and Tom said, "We are very sorry, sir. We were playing. We liked your boot. We did not think. We are sorry. Please forgive us."

The man looked at them. He saw that they were sorry. He said, "Well, I am glad that you are sorry. And I am glad that you gave my boot back. But you should not do that again. You should ask before you touch something that is not yours. That is polite. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom said, "Yes, sir. We understand. We will not do that again. We will be polite. Thank you for forgiving us."

The man said, "You are welcome. Now, go and play. But be careful. And be nice to each other."

Lily and Tom said, "Okay, sir. Thank you. Goodbye."

They ran to the swings. They played together. They were happy. They were friends. They were polite.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big jar of butter in the kitchen. They wanted to spread it on their bread, but they did not have a knife.

"Let me have the butter," Sara said. "I will use my fingers."

"No, I want the butter," Ben said. "I will use my spoon."

They both grabbed the jar and pulled hard. The lid popped off and the butter flew out. It landed on their faces, their hair, their clothes and the floor.

"Look what you did!" Sara yelled. "You are selfish!"

"No, you are selfish!" Ben yelled back. "You started it!"

They were so angry that they did not notice their mom coming in. She saw the mess and gasped.

"What happened here?" she asked. "Why did you waste the butter?"

Sara and Ben felt ashamed. They knew they had been bad. They did not answer their mom.

Mom shook her head. She took a cloth and wiped their faces. Then she took them to the bathroom and washed their hair and clothes. She was not happy.

"You need to learn to share," she said. "Butter is not a toy. It is food. Some people do not have enough food. You should be grateful for what you have."

Sara and Ben nodded. They were sorry. They hugged their mom and said they were sorry.

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She said she loved them. She said they could have some bread and jam instead of butter. She said they could play with their toys after they ate.

Sara and Ben agreed. They said they loved their mom too. They said they would share their bread and jam and their toys. They said they would not be selfish anymore.

They learned their lesson. They did not fight over butter again. They grew up to be kind and generous. They always remembered their mom's words.

"Maybe it is a cake for us!" Jen said.

They ran to the box and tried to open it. But it was too hard. They needed scissors or a knife. They looked around and saw a knife on the table. Tim had an idea.

"I will get the knife and cut the box. You watch for Mom and Dad," he said to Jen.

"OK," Jen said. She felt a little guilty. She knew they were not supposed to touch the knife. But she wanted to see what was in the box.

Tim got the knife and went back to the box. He started to cut the tape. But he was not careful. He cut his finger. He cried out loud.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" he shouted.

Jen heard him and ran to him. She saw the blood on his finger. She was scared.

"Tim, are you OK? What happened?" she asked.

"I cut myself with the knife. It hurts!" he said.

They heard footsteps. Mom and Dad came into the living room. They saw the box, the knife, and the blood. They were angry and worried.

"What are you doing? Why did you touch the knife? How did you hurt yourself?" they asked.

Tim and Jen looked at each other. They felt very guilty. They did not know what to say.

The box was a gift for their grandma. It was her birthday. Mom and Dad had bought her a nice sweater. They wanted to give it to her later that day. But now the box was ripped and the sweater was stained.

Tim and Jen learned a lesson. They should not touch things that are not theirs. They should not use things that are dangerous. They should listen to Mom and Dad. They said sorry to them and to grandma. They gave her a hug and a kiss. They hoped she would forgive them.

Anna and Ben like to play in the bath. They have many toys to make bubbles and splash. They also have a pink duck that can quack. Anna loves the pink duck very much. She always gives it a hug and a kiss.

One day, Anna and Ben are in the bath. They are having fun with the toys and the water. Anna says, "Look, Ben, I can make the pink duck soak. I can fill it with water and squeeze it. Then it makes a big squirt. See?" She shows Ben how she does it.

Ben laughs and says, "That's cool, Anna. Can I try?" He takes the pink duck from Anna and fills it with water. He squeezes it hard. But the pink duck does not squirt. It makes a loud pop. The water comes out from a hole in the duck. The hole is big and the duck is broken.

Anna gasps and says, "Oh no, Ben, you broke my pink duck. My pink duck is my favorite. How can you do that?" She starts to cry. She feels sad and angry.

Ben feels sorry and says, "I'm sorry, Anna. I didn't mean to break your pink duck. I just wanted to play with it. Please don't cry. I'll get you a new pink duck. A better one. A bigger one. A warmer one. This one is cold and wet. You don't want a cold and wet duck, do you?"

Anna sniffles and says, "No, I don't want a cold and wet duck. I want a pink duck. A nice pink duck. A soft pink duck. A quacking pink duck. Like the one you broke."

Ben hugs Anna and says, "I know, Anna. I know. I'll find you a pink duck like that. I promise. I love you, Anna. You're my sister. And I'm sorry."

Anna hugs Ben back and says, "I love you too, Ben. You're my brother. And I forgive you. But please be careful with my toys. They are not for breaking. They are for playing."

They smile and kiss. They finish their bath. They dry themselves with towels. They go to their room. They look for a new pink duck. They hope to find one soon.

Tom and Lily were playing outside in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two buttons for eyes. They were very happy with their snowman.

"Look, Mommy!" Tom shouted. "We made a snowman!"

Mommy came out of the house with a camera. She smiled and took a picture of Tom and Lily and their snowman.

"That's a wonderful snowman!" Mommy said. "You two are very creative. Do you want to come inside and have some hot chocolate?"

"Yes, please!" Lily said. She was feeling cold and thirsty.

"Me too!" Tom said. He was also feeling cold and thirsty.

They ran to the house, but before they went in, they saw something shiny under the snowman's hat. It was a gift wrapped in red paper and tied with a gold ribbon.

"What's that?" Tom asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it's for us!"

They carefully lifted the hat and took the gift. They shook it gently and heard a jingle.

"Let's open it!" Tom said.

"Wait!" Mommy said. "That's a special gift. It's from Santa. He left it here for you last night. He wanted to surprise you."

"Wow!" Tom and Lily said. "Thank you, Santa!"

They tore the paper and opened the box. Inside was a music box with a snow globe. When they wound it up, it played a beautiful song and snowflakes fell on a tiny village.

"It's so pretty!" Lily said.

"It's so cool!" Tom said.

They hugged Mommy and thanked her for the hot chocolate. They took their music box inside and put it on the table. They sat on the couch and watched the snow globe. They felt warm and comfortable. They were very happy with their gift.

Sara loved peaches. They were sweet and juicy and soft. She saw a big basket of peaches on the kitchen table. She wanted to eat one. But Mama said no. Mama said peaches were for dessert, after dinner. Sara had to wait.

Sara was very hungry. She smelled the peaches. They smelled so good. She looked at the peaches. They looked so pretty. She reached for a peach. But Mama saw her. Mama said, "Sara, stop! Don't be naughty. You can't have a peach now. You have to resist."

Sara felt angry. She wanted a peach. She didn't want to resist. She said, "But Mama, I'm hungry. I want a peach. Please, please, please." She whined and cried and stamped her feet.

Mama was firm. She said, "Sara, enough. You have to be patient. You have to be good. You have to listen to Mama. If you eat a peach now, you won't have any dessert later. And you will have a tummy ache. Do you want that?"

Sara thought for a moment. She didn't want a tummy ache. She didn't want to miss dessert. She wanted to be good. She wanted to listen to Mama. She said, "Okay, Mama. I'm sorry. I won't eat a peach now. I will resist. I will wait for dinner. Can I have a hug?"

Mama smiled and hugged Sara. She said, "That's my good girl. I'm proud of you. You did the right thing. You resisted. Now, let's go wash your hands and get ready for dinner. And guess what? We have a special treat for dessert. Peach pie!"

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play with stickers and stamps. They have a big book with many pages. They want to complete the book with stickers and stamps.

One day, they find a new stamp. It is red and round. It has a picture of a star. Tom and Anna are happy. They want to use the stamp on their book.

They open the book and look for a page. They see a page with many shapes. There are circles, squares, triangles, and stars. Tom and Anna think the stamp will fit on the page.

Tom takes the stamp and presses it on the ink pad. He lifts the stamp and moves it to the book. He puts the stamp on a circle. He smiles and says, "Look, I stamped a circle!"

Anna looks at the book. She is confused. She says, "No, Tom, that is not a circle. That is a star. You stamped a star on a circle. That is wrong."

Tom is confused too. He says, "But the stamp is round. It looks like a circle. Why is it a star?"

Anna says, "The stamp is round, but the picture is a star. You have to look at the picture, not the shape. The picture tells you what it is. See, this is a circle, and this is a star."

She points to the shapes on the page. She takes the stamp and presses it on the ink pad. She lifts the stamp and moves it to the book. She puts the stamp on a star. She smiles and says, "Look, I stamped a star on a star. That is right."

Tom looks at the book. He understands now. He says, "Oh, I see. The picture is a star. I was wrong. I'm sorry, Anna."

Anna says, "It's okay, Tom. You can try again. Let's complete the book with stickers and stamps. It will be fun."

Tom and Anna hug. They are friends. They continue to play with stickers and stamps. They complete the book with many colors and pictures. They are happy.

Anna likes to wake up early and go to the bus stop with her mom. She likes to see the big yellow bus that takes her mom to work. She likes to wave goodbye and say "I love you, Mom!"

One day, Anna wakes up and sees that it is raining outside. She puts on her raincoat and boots and goes to the bus stop with her mom. But when they get there, they see that the big yellow bus is not there. Instead, there is a small green bus with funny pictures on it.

"Where is the big yellow bus, Mom?" Anna asks.

"I don't know, sweetie. Maybe it is broken or late. This is a different bus. It is original. It is not like the other buses," her mom says.

"Can we ride on it, Mom?" Anna asks.

"Sure, why not? It might be fun. Let's go and see where it takes us," her mom says.

They get on the small green bus and sit down. The bus driver smiles and says "Hello, welcome to the original bus. Today we are going to the zoo. Are you ready for an adventure?"

Anna and her mom look at each other and smile. They are ready for an adventure. They hold hands and say "Yes, we are!"

Tom and Lily like to collect things. They have a box full of shells, rocks, feathers and stickers. One day, they see a shiny card on the street. It has a picture of a man and some letters and numbers.

"Look, Lily, what is this?" Tom asks, picking up the card.

"I don't know, Tom. Maybe it is a license. It looks like the one Mommy has in her purse," Lily says.

"Can we keep it? Maybe we can trade it for more stickers," Tom says.

"No, Tom, we can't keep it. It belongs to someone else. Maybe they need it to drive a car or go to a store. We should give it back," Lily says.

"But how do we find them, Lily? There are so many people here," Tom says.

"Maybe we can ask a police officer. They help people who are lost or hurt. Come on, Tom, let's go," Lily says.

They hold hands and walk to the corner, where they see a police officer in a blue uniform. He smiles at them and says hello.

"Hello, officer. We found this license on the street. Do you know who it belongs to?" Lily says, showing him the card.

"Wow, you are very honest and kind, kids. This license belongs to Mr. Jones. He lives in that building over there. He must have dropped it by accident. He will be very happy to get it back. Do you want to come with me and return it to him?" the officer says.

"Yes, please. We want to help," Tom and Lily say.

They follow the officer to the building and knock on the door. Mr. Jones opens it and looks surprised.

"Hello, Mr. Jones. I have some visitors for you. They found your license on the street and brought it to me. They wanted to give it back to you," the officer says.

"Really? That's amazing. Thank you so much, kids. You are very smart and brave. I was looking for my license everywhere. I need it to drive to the doctor. I hurt my leg and it hurts a lot. You saved me a lot of trouble. How can I thank you?" Mr. Jones says.

"You're welcome, Mr. Jones. We are glad you are not hurt more. Maybe you can give us a sticker for our collection," Tom says.

"Of course, I can. I have a lot of stickers in my drawer. You can choose any one you like," Mr. Jones says.

He invites them in and gives them each a sticker. They choose a star and a heart. They stick them on their shirts and smile.

"Thank you, Mr. Jones. We hope your leg gets better soon," Lily says.

"Thank you, kids. You are very sweet. And thank you, officer, for bringing them here. You are very helpful," Mr. Jones says.

They say goodbye and leave. The officer gives them a high five and tells them they did a good job. Tom and Lily feel proud and happy. They go back to their box and add their new stickers to their collection. They hug each other and say they are the best collectors ever.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill covered with snow. They wanted to slide down the hill and have fun.

They found a big box and put it on the snow. They climbed inside the box and held on tight. Then they pushed the box with their feet and started to slide.

"Whee!" Lily shouted. "This is fun!"

"Look out!" Ben said. "There is a tree!"

The box was going too fast and they could not stop. They hit the tree and the box broke. Lily and Ben fell out and landed on the icy snow.

"Ow!" Lily cried. "That hurt!"

"Are you okay?" Ben asked.

Lily nodded. She had a bump on her head and a scratch on her arm, but she was not badly hurt. Ben had a bruise on his leg and a tear on his coat, but he was not badly hurt either.

They got up and looked at the broken box. They felt sad. They liked the box and they wanted to slide some more.

"Maybe we can find another box," Lily said.

"Or maybe we can improve our box," Ben said. "We can fix it with tape and make it stronger. And we can steer it with a rope and avoid the tree."

"That sounds like a good idea," Lily said. "Let's try it."

They went to the garage and found some tape and a rope. They worked hard to improve their box. Then they carried it back to the hill and tried it again.

This time, they slid down the hill smoothly and safely. They steered the box with the rope and had fun. They laughed and cheered and enjoyed the icy snow.

They improved their box and had more fun. They were happy and proud. They were good friends who liked to play outside.

Ben and Mia were friends who liked to play together. They had a big pool in their backyard where they could swim and splash. One day, they decided to have a race in the water.

"Ready, set, go!" Ben shouted and started to swim as fast as he could. Mia followed him, but she was slower. Ben reached the other side of the pool and turned around. He saw Mia still swimming and smiled.

"I win, I win!" he said. "I am the best swimmer!"

Mia did not like that. She felt envious of Ben. She wanted to be the best swimmer too. She reached the other side of the pool and got out. She looked at Ben and said, "No, you are not the best swimmer. You cheated. You started before me."

Ben was surprised. He did not cheat. He started when he said go. He looked at Mia and said, "No, I did not cheat. You are just slow. You are a bad swimmer."

Mia and Ben started to argue. They did not agree. They said mean things to each other. They made each other sad and angry.

Their mom heard them and came outside. She saw them fighting and said, "Stop, stop! What is going on? Why are you not playing nicely?"

Mia and Ben told their mom what happened. They blamed each other for the race. Their mom listened and said, "I see. You both wanted to win, but you did not have fun. You let your envy and pride hurt your friendship. That is not good. You should be happy for each other and share your skills. You should say sorry and hug."

Mia and Ben thought about what their mom said. They realized they were wrong. They did not want to lose their friend. They felt sorry and hugged.

"I am sorry, Ben. You are a good swimmer. You did not cheat. Can we be friends again?" Mia said.

"I am sorry, Mia. You are a good swimmer too. You are not slow. Can we be friends again?" Ben said.

Their mom smiled and said, "That is better. Now, why don't you swim together and have fun? You can take turns to be the leader and the follower. You can teach each other new tricks. You can enjoy the pool and the sun."

Mia and Ben agreed. They jumped back into the pool and swam together. They had fun and laughed. They were friends again.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play near the river. The river is big and blue and makes a nice sound. Sometimes they see fish and ducks and frogs in the river.

One day, Tom and Sam find a funny thing by the river. It is round and shiny and has a hole in it. Tom thinks it is a hat. He puts it on his head and says, "Look at me, I am a king!" Sam thinks it is a bowl. He takes it from Tom and says, "No, it is a bowl. I can put water and mud in it and make soup!"

Tom and Sam start to fight over the funny thing. They pull and push and shout at each other. They do not mind the river or the fish or the ducks or the frogs. They only mind the funny thing.

But then, something bad happens. The funny thing slips from their hands and falls into the river. It sinks and disappears. Tom and Sam are sad and sorry. They have lost the funny thing and they have hurt their friendship.

They hug and say, "I am sorry, you are my friend. I do not mind the funny thing. I mind you." They smile and play again. They mind the river and the fish and the ducks and the frogs. They have fun and forget the funny thing. They are happy.

Lily had a bad fall and hurt her arm. She cried a lot and her mom took her to the doctor. The doctor was very kind and said he needed to take a picture of her arm. He called it an x-ray.

"What is an x-ray?" Lily asked.

"It is a special machine that can see your bones. It helps me find out if your arm is broken or not. It will not hurt, I promise. You just need to stay still and stare at the wall for a few seconds," the doctor explained.

Lily was scared, but she trusted the doctor. She followed him to a small room with a big machine. The doctor put a heavy apron on her and told her to lie down on a table. He put her arm on a flat plate and moved the machine over it.

"Ready? One, two, three, smile!" the doctor said and pressed a button. Lily heard a beep and saw a flash of light.

The doctor came back and showed her a paper with a picture of her arm. Lily saw her bones and was amazed.

"Wow, that is brilliant!" she exclaimed.

"Yes, it is. And the good news is, your arm is not broken. You just have a bruise. You can go home and rest. And here is a sticker for being so brave," the doctor said and gave her a smiley face sticker.

Lily was happy and thanked the doctor. She hugged her mom and showed her the x-ray and the sticker. She was proud of herself and her brilliant arm.

Mia liked to play with her toys in the garden. She had a doll, a ball, a car and a book. She made a lot of noise and had a lot of fun. But she did not like to tidy up her toys when she was done. She left them on the grass, on the path, on the bench and on the swing.

One day, a chicken came to the garden. It was a big, brown chicken with a red comb and yellow feet. It saw Mia's toys and thought they were food. It pecked at the doll, the ball, the car and the book. It made a lot of mess and noise. Mia heard the chicken and ran to the garden. She was very angry and scared.

She shouted at the chicken and tried to chase it away. But the chicken was faster and smarter. It ran around the garden and hid behind the toys. Mia could not catch it. She was very tired and sad. She wished she had tidied up her toys.

Then she had an idea. She went to the kitchen and got some bread. She broke it into small pieces and threw them on the grass. The chicken smelled the bread and came out of its hiding place. It followed the bread trail to the gate. Mia quickly closed the gate and locked it. The chicken was gone.

Mia was very happy and relieved. She learned her lesson. She decided to tidy up her toys and put them in a box. She did not want the chicken to come back and ruin them. She settled down on the bench and read her book. She was very quiet and calm.

Lila was a little girl who liked to play in the garden. She liked to dig holes and look for bugs and worms. One day, she saw a small, furry animal with a long nose and tiny eyes. It was a mole. Lila wondered what the mole was doing in her garden. She wanted to be friends with it.

She ran to the mole and said, "Hello, mole! Do you want to play with me? I have a shovel and a bucket. We can dig more holes and find more bugs and worms."

The mole was scared of Lila. He did not want to play with her. He wanted to hide in his hole. He said, "No, no, no! Go away, girl! You are big and loud and scary. You will hurt me and my home. Leave me alone!"

But Lila did not listen to the mole. She thought he was shy and cute. She tried to pick him up and hug him. She said, "Don't be afraid, mole. I will not hurt you. I will be nice to you. You are so soft and warm. You can be my pet."

The mole did not like to be picked up and hugged. He felt trapped and angry. He bit Lila's finger with his sharp teeth. He said, "Let me go, let me go, let me go! You are mean and rude and silly. You do not know how to treat me. I am not your pet. I am a wild animal."

Lila screamed and dropped the mole. She ran to her mom and showed her the bite. She said, "Mom, mom, mom! The mole bit me! It hurt so much. Why did he do that? I just wanted to be his friend."

Her mom looked at the bite and said, "Oh, Lila. You are not lucky. You are foolish. You should not bother the mole. He does not want to be your friend. He wants to be left alone. You should respect his space and his nature. Now we have to go to the doctor and get a shot. Maybe you will learn your lesson."

Lila cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, mole. I did not mean to make you mad. I just wondered what you were like. I will not bother you again."

The mole watched Lila and her mom leave. He was glad they were gone. He went back to his hole and said, "Good riddance, girl. You are not welcome in my garden. I am lucky to be a mole. I do not need friends like you."

"No, I can't. I can only waddle," said the duck.

The end.

Lily rubbed her fingers on the whistle and then blew again. This time, a loud sound came out! "Wow!" said Lily, "I did it!" 

They played for a while longer, but then it started to rain. "Oh no!" said Lily. "I don't want to get my yellow dress wet!" Timmy laughed and said, "Don't worry, we can run under that big tree over there." They ran under the tree and stayed dry until the rain stopped. 

Lily was happy that she got to blow the whistle and keep her yellow dress dry. She hugged Timmy and said, "Thanks for being my friend." Timmy smiled and hugged her back.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Zoom. Zoom loved to go fast and zoom around the town. One day, Zoom ran out of gas and he couldn't go anymore. But then, a kind man came to supply Zoom with gas and he was able to zoom again. 

Zoom drove around and saw a lovely flower on the side of the road. He stopped to look at it and thought it was very pretty. Suddenly, he saw a little bird who needed help. The bird's nest had fallen and the eggs were in danger. Zoom wanted to help, so he went to the store to get some supplies. 

With the supplies, Zoom was able to fix the bird's nest and save the eggs. The little bird was very happy and thanked Zoom. From that day on, Zoom knew that it was important to help others and to always have enough gas to keep zooming around.

But Timmy didn't know how to sing, and he started to shout into the microphone instead. Lily's ears hurt and she said, "Stop! You're too loud!" Timmy got upset and said, "I don't want to play with you anymore!" and ran away.

Lily felt sad and realized that she should have told Timmy how to use the microphone properly instead of just giving it to him. She decided to send him a message and apologize. Timmy forgave her and they became friends again. Lily learned that it's important to be kind and helpful to others.

"Hi there!" replied Bella. "What a beautiful lake you have here. It's so big and blue." 

"Yes, it's my favorite place to come and play," said Lily. "I love to swim in it and look at all the fish." 

"That sounds like so much fun," said Bella. "I wish I could swim, but I guess flying is my special talent."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy saw a funny-looking bug crawling on the ground. He wanted to pick it up and play with it, but his mom had told him that some bugs can be poisonous and dangerous.

Timmy's friend, Billy, came over and saw the bug too. Billy didn't listen to Timmy's warning and picked up the bug. Suddenly, Billy started feeling sick and dizzy. Timmy knew he had to help his friend. He gave Billy a big hug and told him everything would be okay.

Timmy's mom called the doctor, and Billy got the medicine he needed to feel better. Timmy learned that it's important to listen to his mom's warnings about dangerous things, but it's also important to be a good friend and help someone when they need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved candy very much. One day, she got a big bag of candy from her grandma. She was so happy and ate a lot of candy. But then, she left the candy in the sun and it started to melt. Lily was sad because all her candy was ruined. 

Her mom saw her sad face and wanted to make her feel better. She took her to the store and bought her some new candy. Lily was happy again and promised to not leave her candy in the sun anymore. From that day on, she always kept her candy safe and never let it melt again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. The bird liked to fly in the sky. It was very graceful when it flew. One day, the bird flew to a party. At the party, there was a big dessert. The bird wanted to eat the dessert. But, the bird was too full from flying. So, the bird watched everyone else eat the dessert. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a stubborn cat named Mittens. One day, Mittens climbed up a tall tree and couldn't get down. Lily tried to rescue Mittens, but she couldn't climb the tree either.

Lily's mom called the fire department to help rescue Mittens. The firefighters came and saved Mittens from the tree. Mittens was happy to be rescued and cuddled with Lily.

But then, Lily and Mittens went for a walk and saw a bad man. The bad man put Lily in jail and took Mittens away. Lily cried and cried, but no one could rescue her.

Lily never saw Mittens again and missed her very much. She learned that sometimes even when someone is rescued, bad things can still happen.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family who lived by the river. The river was very big and had lots of water. The family loved to play in the river and swim in it. The river was always lively with fish swimming and birds flying.

One day, the family decided to go on a picnic by the river. They woke up early and packed lots of yummy food. When they got to the river, they saw that it was even more lively than usual. There were ducks swimming and children playing.

The family had a great time eating their food and playing by the lively river. They were very happy to be together and to have such a fun day. When it was time to go home, they were tired but very grateful for their special day by the lively river.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red lamp in his room that he loved very much. One day, Timmy's dad told him they needed to sell the lamp because they needed money. Timmy was sad but he didn't want his family to be poor. 

They put the red lamp outside their house with a sign that said "For Sale". A man came and said he would buy the lamp. Timmy's dad sold it to him and they got some money. Timmy was still sad but he knew it was for the best.

The man took the red lamp and left. Later that day, Timmy saw the red lamp in a store window. He was confused and sad because he thought the man wanted to keep it. Timmy learned that sometimes people sell things just to make money and not because they care about them.
